segs.p: Ahañhi, sīha, akiriyaṁ vadāmi kāyaduccaritassa vacīduccaritassa manoduccaritassa;
segs.e: I teach inaction regarding bad bodily, verbal, and mental conduct,

segs.p: anekavihitānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ akiriyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: and the many kinds of unskillful things.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: In this sense you could rightly say that I teach inaction.

segs.p: ‘akiriyavādo samaṇo gotamo, akiriyāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti.
Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: And what’s the sense in which you could rightly say that

segs.p: ‘kiriyavādo samaṇo gotamo, kiriyāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti?
segs.e: I believe in action, I teach action, and I guide my disciples in that way?

segs.p: Ahañhi, sīha, kiriyaṁ vadāmi kāyasucaritassa vacīsucaritassa manosucaritassa;
segs.e: I teach action regarding good bodily, verbal, and mental conduct,
and the many kinds of skillful things.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: In this sense you could rightly say that I teach action.

segs.p: ‘kiriyavādo samaṇo gotamo, kiriyāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti.
Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: And what’s the sense in which you could rightly say that

segs.p: ‘ucchedavādo samaṇo gotamo, ucchedāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti?
segs.e: I believe in annihilationism, I teach annihilation, and I guide my disciples in that way?

segs.p: Ahañhi, sīha, ucchedaṁ vadāmi rāgassa dosassa mohassa;
segs.e: I teach the annihilation of greed, hate, and delusion,

segs.p: anekavihitānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ ucchedaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: and the many kinds of unskillful things.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: In this sense you could rightly say that I teach annihilationism.

segs.p: ‘ucchedavādo samaṇo gotamo, ucchedāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti.
Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: And what’s the sense in which you could rightly say that

segs.p: ‘jegucchī samaṇo gotamo, jegucchitāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti?
segs.e: I’m disgusted, I teach disgust, and I guide my disciples in that way?

segs.p: Ahañhi, sīha, jigucchāmi kāyaduccaritena vacīduccaritena manoduccaritena;
segs.e: I’m disgusted by bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind,

segs.p: jigucchāmi anekavihitānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ samāpattiyā.
segs.e: and by attainment of the many kinds of unskillful things.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: In this sense you could rightly say that I’m disgusted.

segs.p: ‘jegucchī samaṇo gotamo, jegucchitāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti.
Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: And what’s the sense in which you could rightly say that

segs.p: ‘venayiko samaṇo gotamo, vinayāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti?
segs.e: I’m an exterminator, I teach extermination, and I guide my disciples in that way?

segs.p: Ahañhi, sīha, vinayāya dhammaṁ desemi rāgassa dosassa mohassa;
segs.e: I teach the extermination of greed, hate, and delusion,

segs.p: anekavihitānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ vinayāya dhammaṁ desemi.
segs.e: and the many kinds of unskillful things.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: In this sense you could rightly say that I’m an exterminator.

segs.p: ‘venayiko samaṇo gotamo, vinayāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti.
Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: And what’s the sense in which you could rightly say that

segs.p: ‘tapassī samaṇo gotamo, tapassitāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti?
segs.e: I’m a mortifier, I teach mortification, and I guide my disciples in that way?

segs.p: Tapanīyāhaṁ, sīha, pāpake akusale dhamme vadāmi kāyaduccaritaṁ vacīduccaritaṁ manoduccaritaṁ.
segs.e: I say that bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind should be mortified.

segs.p: Yassa kho, sīha, tapanīyā pāpakā akusalā dhammā pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā, tamahaṁ ‘tapassī’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: I say that a mortifier is someone who has given up unskillful qualities that should be mortified. They’ve cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so that they’re unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa kho, sīha, tapanīyā pāpakā akusalā dhammā pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: The Realized One is someone who has given up unskillful qualities that should be mortified. He has cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so that they’re unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: In this sense you could rightly say that I’m a mortifier.

segs.p: ‘tapassī samaṇo gotamo, tapassitāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti.
Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: And what’s the sense in which you could rightly say that

segs.p: ‘apagabbho samaṇo gotamo, apagabbhatāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti?
segs.e: I’m gutless, I teach gutlessness, and I guide my disciples in that way?

segs.p: Yassa kho, sīha, āyatiṁ gabbhaseyyā punabbhavābhinibbatti pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā, tamahaṁ ‘apagabbho’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: I say that a gutless person is someone who has given up future wombs and rebirth into a new state of existence. They’ve cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so that they’re unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa kho, sīha, āyatiṁ gabbhaseyyā punabbhavābhinibbatti pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: The Realized One has given up future wombs and regeneration into a new state of existence. He has cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so that they’re unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: In this sense you could rightly say that I’m gutless.

segs.p: ‘apagabbho samaṇo gotamo, apagabbhatāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti.
Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: And what’s the sense in which you could rightly say that

segs.p: ‘assāsako samaṇo gotamo, assāsāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti?
segs.e: I’m ambitious, I teach ambition, and I guide my disciples in that way?

segs.p: Ahañhi, sīha, assāsako paramena assāsena, assāsāya dhammaṁ desemi, tena ca sāvake vinemi.
segs.e: I’m ambitious to offer solace, the highest solace, I teach solace, and I guide my disciples in that way.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṁ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: In this sense you could rightly say that I’m ambitious.”

segs.p: ‘assāsako samaṇo gotamo, assāsāya dhammaṁ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, sīho senāpati bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, General Sīha said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, sir! Excellent!

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: “Anuviccakāraṁ kho, sīha, karohi. Anuviccakāro tumhādisānaṁ ñātamanussānaṁ sādhu hotī”ti.
segs.e: “Sīha, you should act after careful consideration. It’s good for well-known people such as yourself to act after careful consideration.”

segs.p: “Imināpāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato bhiyyoso mattāya attamano abhiraddho, yaṁ maṁ bhagavā evamāha: ‘anuviccakāraṁ kho, sīha, karohi. Anuviccakāro tumhādisānaṁ ñātamanussānaṁ sādhu hotī’ti.
segs.e: “Now I’m even more delighted and satisfied with the Buddha, since he tells me to act after careful consideration.

segs.p: Mañhi, bhante, aññatitthiyā sāvakaṁ labhitvā kevalakappaṁ vesāliṁ paṭākaṁ parihareyyuṁ:
segs.e: For if the followers of other religions were to gain me as a disciple, they’d carry a banner all over Vesālī, saying:
‘General Sīha has become our disciple!’

segs.p: Atha ca pana bhagavā evamāha: ‘anuviccakāraṁ, sīha, karohi. Anuviccakāro tumhādisānaṁ ñātamanussānaṁ sādhu hotī’ti.
segs.e: And yet the Buddha tells me to act after careful consideration.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bhante, dutiyampi bhagavantaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: For a second time, I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: “Dīgharattaṁ kho te, sīha, nigaṇṭhānaṁ opānabhūtaṁ kulaṁ, yena nesaṁ upagatānaṁ piṇḍakaṁ dātabbaṁ maññeyyāsī”ti.
segs.e: “For a long time now, Sīha, your family has been a well-spring of support for the Jain ascetics. You should consider giving to them when they come.”

segs.p: “Imināpāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato bhiyyoso mattāya attamano abhiraddho, yaṁ maṁ bhagavā evamāha:
segs.e: “Now I’m even more delighted and satisfied with the Buddha, since he tells me to

segs.p: ‘dīgharattaṁ kho te, sīha, nigaṇṭhānaṁ opānabhūtaṁ kulaṁ, yena nesaṁ upagatānaṁ piṇḍakaṁ dātabbaṁ maññeyyāsī’ti.
segs.e: consider giving to the Jain ascetics when they come.
Sir, I have heard that
the ascetic Gotama says this:

segs.p: mayhameva dānaṁ dātabbaṁ, mayhameva sāvakānaṁ dātabbaṁ;
segs.e: ‘Gifts should only be given to me, and to my disciples.

segs.p: mayhameva dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ, na aññesaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ;
segs.e: Only what is given to me is very fruitful, not what is given to others.

segs.p: mayhameva sāvakānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ, na aññesaṁ sāvakānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalan’ti,
segs.e: Only what is given to my disciples is very fruitful, not what is given to the disciples of others.’

segs.p: atha ca pana maṁ bhagavā nigaṇṭhesupi dāne samādapeti.
segs.e: Yet the Buddha encourages me to give to the Jain ascetics.

segs.p: Api ca, bhante, mayamettha kālaṁ jānissāma.
segs.e: Well, sir, we’ll know the proper time for that.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bhante, tatiyampi bhagavantaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: For a third time, I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sīhassa senāpatissa anupubbiṁ kathaṁ kathesi, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: Then the Buddha taught Sīha step by step, with

segs.p: dānakathaṁ sīlakathaṁ saggakathaṁ, kāmānaṁ ādīnavaṁ okāraṁ saṅkilesaṁ nekkhamme ānisaṁsaṁ pakāsesi.
segs.e: a talk on giving, ethical conduct, and heaven. He revealed the drawbacks of sensual pleasures, so sordid and corrupt, and the benefit of renunciation.

segs.p: Yadā bhagavā aññāsi sīhaṁ senāpatiṁ kallacittaṁ muducittaṁ vinīvaraṇacittaṁ udaggacittaṁ pasannacittaṁ, atha yā buddhānaṁ sāmukkaṁsikā dhammadesanā taṁ pakāsesi—
segs.e: And when the Buddha knew that Sīha’s mind was ready, pliable, rid of hindrances, elated, and confident he revealed the special teaching of the Buddhas:
suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṁ vatthaṁ apagatakāḷakaṁ sammadeva rajanaṁ paṭiggaṇheyya;
segs.e: Just as a clean cloth rid of stains would properly absorb dye,

segs.p: evamevaṁ sīhassa senāpatissa tasmiṁyeva āsane virajaṁ vītamalaṁ dhammacakkhuṁ udapādi:
segs.e: in that very seat the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in General Sīha:
“Everything that is liable to arise is liable to cease.”

segs.p: Atha kho sīho senāpati diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṅkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Sīha saw, attained, understood, and fathomed the Dhamma. He went beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, and became self-assured and independent of others regarding the Teacher’s instructions. He said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṁ saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, would the Buddha together with the mendicant Saṅgha please accept tomorrow’s meal from me?”
The Buddha consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho sīho senāpati bhagavato adhivāsanaṁ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, Sīha rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho sīho senāpati aññataraṁ purisaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then Sīha addressed a certain man,
“My man, please find out if there is any meat ready for sale.”

segs.p: Atha kho sīho senāpati tassā rattiyā accayena sake nivesane paṇītaṁ khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyaṁ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṁ ārocāpesi:
segs.e: And when the night had passed General Sīha had delicious fresh and cooked foods prepared in his own home. Then he had the Buddha informed of the time, saying,
“Sir, it’s time. The meal is ready.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sīhassa senāpatissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghena.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to Sīha’s home, where he sat down on the seat spread out together with the Saṅgha of mendicants.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā nigaṇṭhā vesāliyaṁ rathikāya rathikaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ bāhā paggayha kandanti:
segs.e: Now at that time many Jain ascetics in Vesālī went from street to street and from square to square, calling out with raised arms:

segs.p: “ajja sīhena senāpatinā thūlaṁ pasuṁ vadhitvā samaṇassa gotamassa bhattaṁ kataṁ.
segs.e: “Today General Sīha has slaughtered a fat calf for the ascetic Gotama’s meal.

segs.p: Taṁ samaṇo gotamo jānaṁ uddissakataṁ maṁsaṁ paribhuñjati paṭiccakamman”ti.
segs.e: The ascetic Gotama knowingly eats meat prepared specially for him: this is a deed he caused.”

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro puriso yena sīho senāpati tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā sīhassa senāpatissa upakaṇṇake ārocesi:
segs.e: Then a certain person went up to Sīha and whispered in his ear,
“Please sir, you should know this.

segs.p: Ete sambahulā nigaṇṭhā vesāliyaṁ rathikāya rathikaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ bāhā paggayha kandanti:
segs.e: Many Jain ascetics in Vesālī are going from street to street and square to square, calling out with raised arms:

segs.p: ‘ajja sīhena senāpatinā thūlaṁ pasuṁ vadhitvā samaṇassa gotamassa bhattaṁ kataṁ.
segs.e: ‘Today General Sīha has slaughtered a fat calf for the ascetic Gotama’s meal.

segs.p: Taṁ samaṇo gotamo jānaṁ uddissakataṁ maṁsaṁ paribhuñjati paṭiccakamman’ti.
segs.e: The ascetic Gotama knowingly eats meat prepared specially for him: this is a deed he caused.’”

segs.p: Alaṁ ayyo dīgharattañhi te āyasmanto avaṇṇakāmā buddhassa avaṇṇakāmā dhammassa avaṇṇakāmā saṅghassa.
segs.e: “Enough, master. For a long time those venerables have wanted to discredit the Buddha, his teaching, and his Saṅgha.

segs.p: Na ca panete āyasmanto jiridanti taṁ bhagavantaṁ asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhituṁ;
segs.e: They’ll never stop misrepresenting the Buddha with their incorrect, hollow, false, untruthful claims.

segs.p: na ca mayaṁ jīvitahetupi sañcicca pāṇaṁ jīvitā voropeyyāmā”ti.
segs.e: We would never deliberately take the life of a living creature, not even for life’s sake.”

segs.p: Atha kho sīho senāpati buddhappamukhaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi.
segs.e: Then Sīha served and satisfied the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha with his own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Atha kho sīho senāpati bhagavantaṁ bhuttāviṁ onītapattapāṇiṁ ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: When the Buddha had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, Sīha sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho sīhaṁ senāpatiṁ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṁsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmīti.
segs.e: Then the Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired him with a Dhamma talk, after which he rose from his seat and left.
Numbered Discourses 8.13
2. The Great Chapter
A Thoroughbred

segs.p: “Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño bhaddo assājānīyo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a fine royal thoroughbred with eight factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and reckoned a factor of kingship.
What eight?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño bhaddo assājānīyo ubhato sujāto hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a fine royal thoroughbred is well born on both
the mother’s and the father’s sides.

segs.p: Yassaṁ disāyaṁ aññepi bhaddā assājānīyā jāyanti, tassaṁ disāyaṁ jāto hoti.
segs.e: He’s bred in the region fine thoroughbreds come from.
Whatever food he’s given,
fresh or dry,
he eats carefully, without making a mess.

segs.p: Jegucchī hoti uccāraṁ vā passāvaṁ vā abhinisīdituṁ vā abhinipajjituṁ vā.
segs.e: He’s disgusted by sitting or lying down in excrement or urine.

segs.p: Sorato hoti sukhasaṁvāso, na ca aññe asse ubbejetā.
segs.e: He’s gentle and pleasant to live with, and he doesn’t upset the other horses.

segs.p: Yāni kho panassa honti sāṭheyyāni kūṭeyyāni jimheyyāni vaṅkeyyāni, tāni yathābhūtaṁ sārathissa āvikattā hoti.
segs.e: He openly shows his tricks, bluffs, ruses, and feints to his trainer,
so the trainer can try to subdue them.
He carries his load, determining:

segs.p: ‘Kāmaññe assā vahantu vā mā vā, ahamettha vahissāmī’ti cittaṁ uppādeti.
segs.e: ‘Whether or not the other horses carry their loads, I’ll carry mine.’
He always walks in a straight path.

segs.p: Thāmavā hoti yāva jīvitamaraṇapariyādānā thāmaṁ upadaṁsetā.
segs.e: He’s strong, and stays strong even until death.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño bhaddo assājānīyo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: A fine royal thoroughbred with these eight factors is worthy of a king. …

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with eight qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What eight?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.
Whatever food they’re given,
coarse or fine,
they eat carefully, without bother.
They’re disgusted with bad conduct by way of body, speech, or mind,

segs.p: jegucchī hoti anekavihitānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ samāpattiyā.
segs.e: and by attainment of the many kinds of unskillful things.

segs.p: Sorato hoti sukhasaṁvāso, na aññe bhikkhū ubbejetā.
segs.e: They’re gentle and pleasant to live with, and they don’t upset the other mendicants.

segs.p: Yāni kho panassa honti sāṭheyyāni kūṭeyyāni jimheyyāni vaṅkeyyāni, tāni yathābhūtaṁ āvikattā hoti satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu.
segs.e: They openly show their tricks, bluffs, ruses, and feints to their sensible spiritual companions,

segs.p: Tesamassa satthā vā viññū vā sabrahmacārī abhinimmadanāya vāyamati.
segs.e: so they can try to subdue them.
They do their training, determining:

segs.p: ‘Kāmaññe bhikkhū sikkhantu vā mā vā, ahamettha sikkhissāmī’ti cittaṁ uppādeti.
segs.e: ‘Whether or not the other mendicants do their training, I’ll do mine.’
They always walk in a straight path.
And here the straight path is
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.
They’re energetic:

segs.p: ‘kāmaṁ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhi ca avasissatu, sarīre upassussatu maṁsalohitaṁ; yaṁ taṁ purisathāmena purisavīriyena purisaparakkamena pattabbaṁ, na taṁ apāpuṇitvā vīriyassa saṇṭhānaṁ bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Gladly, let my skin, sinews, and bones remain! Let the blood and flesh waste away in my body! I will not stop trying until I have achieved what is possible by human strength, energy, and vigor.’

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these eight qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 8.14
2. The Great Chapter
A Wild Colt

segs.p: “Aṭṭha ca, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅke desessāmi aṭṭha ca assadose, aṭṭha ca purisakhaḷuṅke aṭṭha ca purisadose.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you about eight wild colts and eight defects in horses, and about eight wild people and eight defects in people.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Katame ca, bhikkhave, aṭṭha assakhaḷuṅkā aṭṭha ca assadosā?
segs.e: “And what, mendicants, are the eight wild colts and eight defects in horses?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā pacchato paṭikkamati, piṭṭhito rathaṁ pavatteti.
segs.e: Firstly, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, some wild colts back right up and spin the chariot behind them.
Some wild colts are like that.
This is the first defect of a horse.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā pacchā laṅghati, kubbaraṁ hanati, tidaṇḍaṁ bhañjati.
segs.e: Furthermore, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, some wild colts jump back, wreck the hub, and break the triple rod.
Some wild colts are like that.
This is the second defect of a horse.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā rathīsāya satthiṁ ussajjitvā rathīsaṁyeva ajjhomaddati.
segs.e: Furthermore, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, some wild colts shake the draft-pole off their thigh and trample it.
Some wild colts are like that.
This is the third defect of a horse.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā ummaggaṁ gaṇhati, ubbaṭumaṁ rathaṁ karoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, some wild colts take a wrong turn, sending the chariot off track.
Some wild colts are like that.
This is the fourth defect of a horse.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā laṅghati purimakāyaṁ paggaṇhati purime pāde.
segs.e: Furthermore, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, some wild colts rear up and strike out with their fore-legs.
Some wild colts are like that.
This is the fifth defect of a horse.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā anādiyitvā sārathiṁ anādiyitvā patodalaṭṭhiṁ dantehi mukhādhānaṁ vidhaṁsitvā yena kāmaṁ pakkamati.
segs.e: Furthermore, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, some wild colts ignore the trainer and the goad, spit out the bit, and go wherever they want.
Some wild colts are like that.
This is the sixth defect of a horse.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā neva abhikkamati no paṭikkamati tattheva khīlaṭṭhāyī ṭhito hoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, some wild colts don’t step forward or turn back but stand right there still as a post.
Some wild colts are like that.
This is the seventh defect of a horse.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā purime ca pāde saṁharitvā pacchime ca pāde saṁharitvā tattheva cattāro pāde abhinisīdati.
segs.e: Furthermore, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, some wild colts tuck in their fore-legs and hind-legs, and sit right down on their four legs.
Some wild colts are like that.
This is the eighth defect of a horse.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha assakhaḷuṅkā aṭṭha ca assadosā.
segs.e: These are the eight wild colts and the eight defects in horses.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, aṭṭha purisakhaḷuṅkā aṭṭha ca purisadosā?
segs.e: And what are the eight wild people and eight defects in people?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṁ āpattiyā codenti.
segs.e: Firstly, the mendicants accuse a mendicant of an offense.

segs.p: So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno ‘na sarāmī’ti asatiyā nibbeṭheti.
segs.e: But the accused mendicant evades it by saying they don’t remember.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā pacchato paṭikkamati, piṭṭhito rathaṁ vatteti;
segs.e: I say that this individual is comparable to the wild colts who, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, back right up and spin the chariot behind them.
Some wild people are like that.
This is the first defect of a person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṁ āpattiyā codenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants accuse a mendicant of an offense.

segs.p: So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno codakaṁyeva paṭippharati:
segs.e: But the accused mendicant objects to the accuser:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho tuyhaṁ bālassa abyattassa bhaṇitena.
segs.e: ‘What has an incompetent fool like you got to say?
How on earth could you imagine you’ve got something worth saying!’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā pacchā laṅghati, kubbaraṁ hanati, tidaṇḍaṁ bhañjati;
segs.e: I say that this individual is comparable to the wild colts who, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, jump back, wreck the hub, and break the triple rod.
Some wild people are like that.
This is the second defect of a person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṁ āpattiyā codenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants accuse a mendicant of an offense.

segs.p: So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno codakasseva paccāropeti:
segs.e: But the accused mendicant retorts to the accuser:

segs.p: ‘tvaṁ khosi itthannāmaṁ āpattiṁ āpanno, tvaṁ tāva paṭhamaṁ paṭikarohī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Well, you’ve fallen into an offense named such-and-such. You should deal with that first.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā rathīsāya satthiṁ ussajjitvā rathīsaṁyeva ajjhomaddati;
segs.e: I say that this individual is comparable to the wild colts who, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, shake the draft-pole off their thigh and trample it.
Some wild people are like that.
This is the third defect of a person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṁ āpattiyā codenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants accuse a mendicant of an offense.

segs.p: So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno aññenāññaṁ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṁ apanāmeti, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: But the accused mendicant dodges the issue, distracts the discussion with irrelevant points, and displays annoyance, hate, and bitterness.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā ummaggaṁ gaṇhati, ubbaṭumaṁ rathaṁ karoti;
segs.e: I say that this individual is comparable to the wild colts who, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, take a wrong turn, sending the chariot off track.
Some wild people are like that.
This is the fourth defect of a person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṁ āpattiyā codenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants accuse a mendicant of an offense.

segs.p: So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno saṅghamajjhe bāhuvikkhepaṁ karoti.
segs.e: But the accused mendicant gesticulates while speaking in the middle of the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā laṅghati, purimakāyaṁ paggaṇhati purime pāde;
segs.e: I say that this individual is comparable to the wild colts who, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, rear up and strike out with their fore-legs.
Some wild people are like that.
This is the fifth defect of a person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṁ āpattiyā codenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants accuse a mendicant of an offense.

segs.p: So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno anādiyitvā saṅghaṁ anādiyitvā codakaṁ sāpattikova yena kāmaṁ pakkamati.
segs.e: But the accused mendicant ignores the Saṅgha and the accusation and, though still guilty of the offense, they go wherever they want.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā anādiyitvā sārathiṁ anādiyitvā patodalaṭṭhiṁ dantehi mukhādhānaṁ vidhaṁsitvā yena kāmaṁ pakkamati;
segs.e: I say that this individual is comparable to the wild colts who, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, ignore the trainer and the goad, spit out the bit, and go wherever they want.
Some wild people are like that.
This is the sixth defect of a person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṁ āpattiyā codenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants accuse a mendicant of an offense.

segs.p: So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno ‘nevāhaṁ āpannomhi, na panāhaṁ āpannomhī’ti so tuṇhībhāvena saṅghaṁ viheṭheti.
segs.e: But the accused mendicant neither confesses to the offense nor denies it, but frustrates the Saṅgha by staying silent.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā neva abhikkamati no paṭikkamati tattheva khīlaṭṭhāyī ṭhito hoti;
segs.e: I say that this individual is comparable to the wild colts who, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, don’t step forward or turn back but stand right there still as a post.
Some wild people are like that.
This is the seventh defect of a person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhikkhuṁ āpattiyā codenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants accuse a mendicant of an offense.

segs.p: So bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno evamāha:
segs.e: But the accused mendicant says this:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho tumhe āyasmanto atibāḷhaṁ mayi byāvaṭā yāva idānāhaṁ sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Why are you venerables making so much of an issue over me? Now I’ll resign the training and return to a lesser life.’
When they have resigned the training, they say:
‘Well, venerables, are you happy now?’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅko ‘pehī’ti vutto, viddho samāno codito sārathinā purime ca pāde saṁharitvā pacchime ca pāde saṁharitvā tattheva cattāro pāde abhinisīdati;
segs.e: I say that this individual is comparable to the wild colts who, when the trainer says ‘giddyup!’ and spurs and goads them on, tuck in their fore-legs and hind-legs, and sit right down on their four legs.
Some wild people are like that.
This is the eighth defect of a person.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha purisakhaḷuṅkā aṭṭha ca purisadosā”ti.
segs.e: These are the eight wild people and eight defects in people.”
Numbered Discourses 8.15
2. The Great Chapter
Stains
“Mendicants, there are these eight stains.
What eight?
Not rehearsing is the stain of hymns.
Neglect is the stain of houses.
Laziness is the stain of beauty.
Negligence is a guard’s stain.
Misconduct is a woman’s stain.
Stinginess is a giver’s stain.

segs.p: malā, bhikkhave, pāpakā akusalā dhammā asmiṁ loke paramhi ca;
segs.e: Bad, unskillful qualities are a stain in this world and the next.

segs.p: tato, bhikkhave, malā malataraṁ avijjā paramaṁ malaṁ.
segs.e: Worse than any of these is ignorance, the worst stain of all.
These are the eight stains.
Not rehearsing is the stain of hymns.
The stain of houses is neglect.
Laziness is the stain of beauty.
A guard’s stain is negligence.
Misconduct is a woman’s stain.
A giver’s stain is stinginess.
Bad qualities are a stain
in this world and the next.
But a worse stain than these
is ignorance, the worst stain of all.”
Numbered Discourses 8.16
2. The Great Chapter
Going on a Mission

segs.p: “Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu dūteyyaṁ gantumarahati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with eight qualities is worthy of going on a mission.
What eight?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sotā ca hoti, sāvetā ca, uggahetā ca, dhāretā ca, viññātā ca, viññāpetā ca, kusalo ca sahitāsahitassa, no ca kalahakārako—
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who learns and educates others. They memorize and remember. They understand and help others understand. They’re skilled at knowing what’s on topic and what isn’t. And they don’t cause quarrels.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu dūteyyaṁ gantumarahati.
segs.e: A mendicant with these eight qualities is worthy of going on a mission.

segs.p: Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato sāriputto dūteyyaṁ gantumarahati.
segs.e: Having eight qualities Sāriputta is worthy of going on a mission.
What eight?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, sāriputto sotā ca hoti, sāvetā ca, uggahetā ca, dhāretā ca, viññātā ca, viññāpetā ca, kusalo ca sahitāsahitassa, no ca kalahakārako.
segs.e: He learns and educates others. He memorizes and remembers. He understands and helps others understand. He’s skilled at knowing what’s on topic and what isn’t. And he doesn’t cause quarrels.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahi dhammehi samannāgato sāriputto dūteyyaṁ gantumarahatīti.
segs.e: Having these eight qualities Sāriputta is worthy of going on a mission.
They don’t tremble when arriving
at an assembly of fierce debaters.
They don’t miss out any words,
or conceal the instructions.
Their words aren’t poisoned,
and they don’t tremble when questioned.
Such a mendicant
is worthy of going on a mission.”
Numbered Discourses 8.17
2. The Great Chapter
Catching (1st)
“Mendicants, a woman catches a man using eight features.
What eight?
With weeping,
laughing,
speaking,
appearance,
gifts of wildflowers,
scents,
tastes,
and touches.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahākārehi itthī purisaṁ bandhati.
segs.e: A woman catches a man using these eight features.

segs.p: Te, bhikkhave, sattā subaddhā, ye phassena baddhā”ti.
segs.e: But those beings who are caught by touch are well and truly caught.”
Numbered Discourses 8.18
2. The Great Chapter
Catching (2nd)
“Mendicants, a man catches a woman using eight features.
What eight?
With weeping,
laughing,
speaking,
appearance,
gifts of wildflowers,
scents,
tastes,
and touches.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahākārehi puriso itthiṁ bandhati.
segs.e: A man catches a woman using these eight features.

segs.p: Te, bhikkhave, sattā subaddhā, ye phassena baddhā”ti.
segs.e: But those beings who are caught by touch are well and truly caught.”
Numbered Discourses 8.19
2. The Great Chapter
With Pahārāda

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā verañjāyaṁ viharati naḷerupucimandamūle.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in Verañjā at the root of a neem tree dedicated to Naḷeru.

segs.p: Atha kho pahārādo asurindo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ kho pahārādaṁ asurindaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Pahārāda, lord of titans, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side. The Buddha said to him,
“Well, Pahārāda, do the titans love the ocean?”
“Sir, they do indeed.”

segs.p: “Kati pana, pahārāda, mahāsamudde acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramantī”ti?
segs.e: “But seeing what incredible and amazing things do the titans love the ocean?”

segs.p: “Aṭṭha, bhante, mahāsamudde acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: “Sir, seeing eight incredible and amazing things the titans love the ocean.
What eight?

segs.p: Mahāsamuddo, bhante, anupubbaninno anupubbapoṇo anupubbapabbhāro, na āyatakeneva papāto.
segs.e: The ocean gradually slants, slopes, and inclines, with no abrupt precipice.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, mahāsamuddo anupubbaninno anupubbapoṇo anupubbapabbhāro, na āyatakeneva papāto;
ayaṁ, bhante, mahāsamudde paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the first thing the titans love about the ocean.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, mahāsamuddo ṭhitadhammo velaṁ nātivattati.
segs.e: Furthermore, the ocean is consistent and doesn’t overflow its boundaries.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, mahāsamuddo ṭhitadhammo velaṁ nātivattati;
ayaṁ, bhante, mahāsamudde dutiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the second thing the titans love about the ocean.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, mahāsamuddo na matena kuṇapena saṁvasati. Yaṁ hoti mahāsamudde mataṁ kuṇapaṁ, taṁ khippameva tīraṁ vāheti, thalaṁ ussāreti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the ocean doesn’t accommodate a carcass, but quickly carries it to the shore and strands it on the beach.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, mahāsamuddo na matena kuṇapena saṁvasati, yaṁ hoti mahāsamudde mataṁ kuṇapaṁ, taṁ khippameva tīraṁ vāheti, thalaṁ ussāreti;
ayaṁ, bhante, mahāsamudde tatiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the third thing the titans love about the ocean.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, yā kāci mahānadiyo, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: Furthermore, when they reach the ocean, all the great rivers—that is,

segs.p: gaṅgā yamunā aciravatī sarabhū mahī, tā mahāsamuddaṁ patvā jahanti purimāni nāmagottāni, ‘mahāsamuddo’ tveva saṅkhaṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—lose their names and clans and are simply reckoned as ‘the ocean’.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, yā kāci mahānadiyo, seyyathidaṁ—gaṅgā yamunā aciravatī sarabhū mahī, tā mahāsamuddaṁ patvā jahanti purimāni nāmagottāni, ‘mahāsamuddo’ tveva saṅkhaṁ gacchanti;
ayaṁ, bhante, mahāsamudde catuttho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing the titans love about the ocean.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, yā ca loke savantiyo mahāsamuddaṁ appenti yā ca antalikkhā dhārā papatanti, na tena mahāsamuddassa ūnattaṁ vā pūrattaṁ vā paññāyati.
segs.e: Furthermore, for all the world’s streams that reach it, and the showers that fall from the sky, the ocean never empties or fills up.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, yā ca loke savantiyo mahāsamuddaṁ appenti yā ca antalikkhā dhārā papatanti, na tena mahāsamuddassa ūnattaṁ vā pūrattaṁ vā paññāyati;
ayaṁ, bhante, mahāsamudde pañcamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the fifth thing the titans love about the ocean.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, mahāsamuddo ekaraso loṇaraso.
segs.e: Furthermore, the ocean has just one taste, the taste of salt.

segs.p: ayaṁ, bhante, mahāsamudde chaṭṭho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the sixth thing the titans love about the ocean.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, mahāsamuddo bahuratano anekaratano. Tatrimāni ratanāni, seyyathidaṁ—muttā maṇi veḷuriyo saṅkho silā pavāḷaṁ rajataṁ jātarūpaṁ lohitako masāragallaṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, the ocean is full of many kinds of treasures, such as pearls, gems, beryl, conch, quartz, coral, silver, native gold, rubies, and emeralds.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, mahāsamuddo bahuratano anekaratano; tatrimāni ratanāni, seyyathidaṁ—muttā maṇi veḷuriyo saṅkho silā pavāḷaṁ rajataṁ jātarūpaṁ lohitako masāragallaṁ;
ayaṁ, bhante, mahāsamudde sattamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the seventh thing the titans love about the ocean.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhante, mahāsamuddo mahataṁ bhūtānaṁ āvāso. Tatrime bhūtā—timi timiṅgalo timirapiṅgalo asurā nāgā gandhabbā. Santi mahāsamudde yojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, dviyojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, tiyojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, catuyojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, pañcayojanasatikāpi attabhāvā.
segs.e: Furthermore, many great beings live in the ocean, such as leviathans, leviathan-gulpers, leviathan-gulper-gulpers, titans, dragons, and centaurs. In the ocean there are life-forms a hundred leagues long, or even two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, or five hundred leagues long.

segs.p: Yampi, bhante, mahāsamuddo mahataṁ bhūtānaṁ āvāso; tatrime bhūtā—timi timiṅgalo timirapiṅgalo asurā nāgā gandhabbā; santi mahāsamudde yojanasatikāpi attabhāvā …pe… tiyojana … catuyojana … pañcayojanasatikāpi attabhāvā;
ayaṁ, bhante, mahāsamudde aṭṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the eighth thing the titans love about the ocean.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhante, mahāsamudde aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramantīti.
segs.e: Seeing these eight incredible and amazing things the titans love the ocean.

segs.p: Api pana, bhante, bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramantī”ti?
segs.e: Well, sir, do the mendicants love this teaching and training?”
“They do indeed, Pahārāda.”

segs.p: “Kati pana, bhante, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramantī”ti?
segs.e: “But seeing how many incredible and amazing things do the mendicants love this teaching and training?”

segs.p: “Aṭṭha, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: “Seeing eight incredible and amazing things, Pahārāda, the mendicants love this teaching and training.
What eight?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, pahārāda, mahāsamuddo anupubbaninno anupubbapoṇo anupubbapabbhāro, na āyatakeneva papāto;
segs.e: The ocean gradually slants, slopes, and inclines, with no abrupt precipice.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā, na āyatakeneva aññāpaṭivedho.
segs.e: In the same way in this teaching and training the penetration to enlightenment comes from gradual training, progress, and practice, not abruptly.

segs.p: Yampi, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā, na āyatakeneva aññāpaṭivedho;
ayaṁ, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the first thing the mendicants love about this teaching and training.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, pahārāda, mahāsamuddo ṭhitadhammo velaṁ nātivattati;
segs.e: The ocean is consistent and doesn’t overflow its boundaries.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, pahārāda, yaṁ mayā sāvakānaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ paññattaṁ taṁ mama sāvakā jīvitahetupi nātikkamanti.
segs.e: In the same way, when a training rule is laid down for my disciples they wouldn’t break it even for the sake of their own life.

segs.p: Yampi, pahārāda, mayā sāvakānaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ paññattaṁ taṁ mama sāvakā jīvitahetupi nātikkamanti;
ayaṁ, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye dutiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the second thing the mendicants love about this teaching and training.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, pahārāda, mahāsamuddo na matena kuṇapena saṁvasati. Yaṁ hoti mahāsamudde mataṁ kuṇapaṁ, taṁ khippameva tīraṁ vāheti thalaṁ ussāreti;
segs.e: The ocean doesn’t accommodate a carcass, but quickly carries it to the shore and strands it on the beach.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, pahārāda, yo so puggalo dussīlo pāpadhammo asucisaṅkassarasamācāro paṭicchannakammanto assamaṇo samaṇapaṭiñño abrahmacārī brahmacāripaṭiñño antopūti avassuto kasambujāto, na tena saṅgho saṁvasati; khippameva naṁ sannipatitvā ukkhipati. Kiñcāpi so hoti majjhe bhikkhusaṅghassa sannisinno, atha kho so ārakāva saṅghamhā saṅgho ca tena.
segs.e: In the same way, the Saṅgha doesn’t accommodate an individual who is unethical, of bad qualities, filthy, with suspicious behavior, underhand, no true ascetic or spiritual practitioner—though claiming to be one—rotten inside, festering, and depraved. But they quickly gather and expel them. Even if they are sitting in the middle of the Saṅgha, they’re far from the Saṅgha, and the Saṅgha is far from them.

segs.p: Yampi, pahārāda, yo so puggalo dussīlo pāpadhammo asucisaṅkassarasamācāro paṭicchannakammanto assamaṇo samaṇapaṭiñño abrahmacārī brahmacāripaṭiñño antopūti avassuto kasambujāto, na tena saṅgho saṁvasati; khippameva naṁ sannipatitvā ukkhipati; kiñcāpi so hoti majjhe bhikkhusaṅghassa sannisinno, atha kho so ārakāva saṅghamhā saṅgho ca tena;
ayaṁ, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye tatiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the third thing the mendicants love about this teaching and training.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, pahārāda, yā kāci mahānadiyo, seyyathidaṁ—gaṅgā yamunā aciravatī sarabhū mahī, tā mahāsamuddaṁ patvā jahanti purimāni nāmagottāni, ‘mahāsamuddo’ tveva saṅkhaṁ gacchanti;
segs.e: When they reach the ocean, all the great rivers—that is, the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—lose their names and clans and are simply reckoned as ‘the ocean’.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, pahārāda, cattārome vaṇṇā—khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā, te tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitvā jahanti purimāni nāmagottāni, ‘samaṇā sakyaputtiyā’ tveva saṅkhaṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: In the same way, when they go forth from the lay life to homelessness, all four classes—aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, and menials—lose their former names and clans and are simply reckoned as ‘ascetics who follow the Sakyan’.

segs.p: Yampi, pahārāda, cattārome vaṇṇā—khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā, te tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitvā jahanti purimāni nāmagottāni, ‘samaṇā sakyaputtiyā’ tveva saṅkhaṁ gacchanti;
ayaṁ, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye catuttho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing the mendicants love about this teaching and training.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, pahārāda, yā ca loke savantiyo mahāsamuddaṁ appenti yā ca antalikkhā dhārā papatanti, na tena mahāsamuddassa ūnattaṁ vā pūrattaṁ vā paññāyati;
segs.e: For all the world’s streams that reach it, and the showers that fall from the sky, the ocean never empties or fills up.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, pahārāda, bahū cepi bhikkhū anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyanti, na tena nibbānadhātuyā ūnattaṁ vā pūrattaṁ vā paññāyati.
segs.e: In the same way, though several mendicants become fully extinguished in the element of extinguishment with no residue, the element of extinguishment never empties or fills up.

segs.p: Yampi, pahārāda, bahū cepi bhikkhū anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyanti, na tena nibbānadhātuyā ūnattaṁ vā pūrattaṁ vā paññāyati;
ayaṁ, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye pañcamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the fifth thing the mendicants love about this teaching and training.
The ocean has just one taste, the taste of salt.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, pahārāda, ayaṁ dhammavinayo ekaraso, vimuttiraso.
segs.e: In the same way, this teaching and training has one taste, the taste of freedom.

segs.p: Yampi, pahārāda, ayaṁ dhammavinayo ekaraso, vimuttiraso;
ayaṁ, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye chaṭṭho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the sixth thing the mendicants love about this teaching and training.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, pahārāda, mahāsamuddo bahuratano anekaratano; tatrimāni ratanāni, seyyathidaṁ—muttā maṇi veḷuriyo saṅkho silā pavāḷaṁ rajataṁ jātarūpaṁ lohitako masāragallaṁ;
segs.e: The ocean is full of many kinds of treasures, such as pearls, gems, beryl, conch, quartz, coral, silver, native gold, rubies, and emeralds.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, pahārāda, ayaṁ dhammavinayo bahuratano anekaratano. Tatrimāni ratanāni, seyyathidaṁ—cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅgā, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo.
segs.e: In the same way, this teaching and training is full of many kinds of treasures, such as the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, and the noble eightfold path.

segs.p: Yampi, pahārāda, ayaṁ dhammavinayo bahuratano anekaratano; tatrimāni ratanāni, seyyathidaṁ—cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅgā, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo;
ayaṁ, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye sattamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the seventh thing the mendicants love about this teaching and training.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, pahārāda, mahāsamuddo mahataṁ bhūtānaṁ āvāso; tatrime bhūtā—timi timiṅgalo timirapiṅgalo asurā nāgā gandhabbā; santi mahāsamudde yojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, dviyojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, tiyojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, catuyojanasatikāpi attabhāvā, pañcayojanasatikāpi attabhāvā;
segs.e: Many great beings live in the ocean, such as leviathans, leviathan-gulpers, leviathan-gulper-gulpers, titans, dragons, and centaurs. In the ocean there are life-forms a hundred leagues long, or even two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, or five hundred leagues long.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, pahārāda, ayaṁ dhammavinayo mahataṁ bhūtānaṁ āvāso; tatrime bhūtā—sotāpanno sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, anāgāmī anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, arahā arahattāya paṭipanno.
segs.e: In the same way, great beings live in this teaching and training, and these are those beings. The stream-enterer and the one practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry. The once-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of once-return. The non-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of non-return. The perfected one, and the one practicing for perfection.

segs.p: Yampi, pahārāda, ayaṁ dhammavinayo mahataṁ bhūtānaṁ āvāso; tatrime bhūtā—sotāpanno sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, anāgāmī anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, arahā arahattāya paṭipanno;
ayaṁ, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye aṭṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the eighth thing the mendicants love about this teaching and training.

segs.p: Ime kho, pahārāda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramantī”ti.
segs.e: Seeing these eight incredible and amazing things, Pahārāda, the mendicants love this teaching and training.”
Numbered Discourses 8.20
2. The Great Chapter
Sabbath

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā tadahuposathe bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto nisinno hoti.
segs.e: Now, at that time it was the sabbath, and the Buddha was sitting surrounded by the Saṅgha of monks.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando abhikkantāya rattiyā, nikkhante paṭhame yāme, uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṁ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And then, as the night was getting late, in the first watch of the night, Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha and said,

segs.p: “abhikkantā, bhante, ratti, nikkhanto paṭhamo yāmo, ciranisinno bhikkhusaṅgho.
segs.e: “Sir, the night is getting late. It is the first watch of the night, and the Saṅgha of monks has been sitting long.
Please, sir, may the Buddha recite the monastic code to the monks.”
But when he said this, the Buddha kept silent.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmā ānando abhikkantāya rattiyā, nikkhante majjhime yāme, uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṁ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time, as the night was getting late, in the middle watch of the night, Ānanda rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha and said,

segs.p: “abhikkantā, bhante, ratti, nikkhanto majjhimo yāmo, ciranisinno bhikkhusaṅgho.
segs.e: “Sir, the night is getting late. It is the middle watch of the night, and the Saṅgha of monks has been sitting long.
Please, sir, may the Buddha recite the monastic code to the monks.”
But for a second time the Buddha kept silent.

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando abhikkantāya rattiyā, nikkhante pacchime yāme, uddhaste aruṇe, nandimukhiyā rattiyā uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṁ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time, as the night was getting late, in the last watch of the night, as dawn stirred, bringing joy to the night, Ānanda rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha and said,

segs.p: “abhikkantā, bhante, ratti, nikkhanto pacchimo yāmo, uddhastaṁ aruṇaṁ, nandimukhī ratti;
segs.e: “Sir, the night is getting late. It is the last watch of the night and dawn stirs, bringing joy to the night.
And the Saṅgha has been sitting long.
Please, sir, may the Buddha recite the monastic code to the monks.”
“Ānanda, the assembly is not pure.”
Then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna thought,

segs.p: “kaṁ nu kho bhagavā puggalaṁ sandhāya evamāha:
segs.e: “Who is the Buddha talking about?”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno sabbāvantaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ cetasā ceto paricca manasākāsi.
segs.e: Then he focused on encompassing the minds of everyone in the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Addasā kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṁ puggalaṁ dussīlaṁ pāpadhammaṁ asuciṁ saṅkassarasamācāraṁ paṭicchannakammantaṁ assamaṇaṁ samaṇapaṭiññaṁ abrahmacāriṁ brahmacāripaṭiññaṁ antopūtiṁ avassutaṁ kasambujātaṁ majjhe bhikkhusaṅghassa nisinnaṁ;
segs.e: He saw that unethical individual, of bad qualities, filthy, with suspicious behavior, underhand, no true ascetic or spiritual practitioner—though claiming to be one—rotten inside, festering, and depraved, sitting in the middle of the Saṅgha.

segs.p: disvāna uṭṭhāyāsanā yena so puggalo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ puggalaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he saw him he rose from his seat, went up to him and said,
“Get up, reverend. The Buddha has seen you.
You can’t live in communion with the monks.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, so puggalo tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: But when he said this, that individual kept silent.

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṁ puggalaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho so puggalo tuṇhī ahosi.
Tatiyampi kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṁ puggalaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and a third time,
he asked that monk to leave.

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho so puggalo tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: But for a third time that individual kept silent.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṁ puggalaṁ bāhāyaṁ gahetvā bahidvārakoṭṭhakā nikkhāmetvā sūcighaṭikaṁ datvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna took that individual by the arm, ejected him out the gate, and bolted the door. Then he went up to the Buddha, and said to him,
“I have ejected that individual.
The assembly is pure.
Please, sir, may the Buddha recite the monastic code to the monks.”
“It’s incredible, Moggallāna, it’s amazing,

segs.p: Yāva bāhā gahaṇāpi nāma so moghapuriso āgamissatī”ti.
segs.e: how that futile man waited to be taken by the arm!”
Then the Buddha said to the monks:

segs.p: “tumheva dāni, bhikkhave, uposathaṁ kareyyātha, pātimokkhaṁ uddiseyyātha.
segs.e: “Now, monks, you should perform the sabbath and recite the monastic code.

segs.p: Na dānāhaṁ, bhikkhave, ajjatagge uposathaṁ karissāmi, pātimokkhaṁ uddisissāmi.
segs.e: From this day forth, I will not perform the sabbath or recite the monastic code.

segs.p: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ tathāgato aparisuddhāya parisāya pātimokkhaṁ uddiseyya.
segs.e: It’s impossible, monks, it can’t happen that a Realized One could recite the monastic code in an impure assembly.

segs.p: Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: Seeing these eight incredible and amazing things the titans love the ocean.
What eight?

segs.p: Mahāsamuddo, bhikkhave, anupubbaninno anupubbapoṇo anupubbapabbhāro, na āyatakeneva papāto.
segs.e: The ocean gradually slants, slopes, and inclines, with no abrupt precipice.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo anupubbaninno anupubbapoṇo anupubbapabbhāro, na āyatakeneva papāto;
ayaṁ, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti (yathā purime tathā vitthāro.)
segs.e: This is the first thing the titans love about the ocean.
(Tell in full as in the previous discourse.)

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo mahataṁ bhūtānaṁ āvāso. Tatrime bhūtā—timi timiṅgalo timirapiṅgalo asurā nāgā gandhabbā. Vasanti mahāsamudde yojanasatikāpi attabhāvā …pe… pañcayojanasatikāpi attabhāvā.
segs.e: Furthermore, many great beings live in the ocean, such as leviathans, leviathan-gulpers, leviathan-gulper-gulpers, titans, dragons, and centaurs. In the ocean there are life-forms a hundred leagues long, or even two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, or five hundred leagues long.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo mahataṁ bhūtānaṁ āvāso; tatrime bhūtā—timi timiṅgalo timirapiṅgalo asurā nāgā gandhabbā; vasanti mahāsamudde yojanasatikāpi attabhāvā …pe… pañcayojanasatikāpi attabhāvā;
ayaṁ, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde aṭṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the eighth thing the titans love about the ocean.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, yaṁ disvā disvā asurā mahāsamudde abhiramanti.
segs.e: Seeing these eight incredible and amazing things the titans love the ocean.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha imasmiṁ dhammavinaye acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: In the same way, seeing eight incredible and amazing things, monks, the mendicants love this teaching and training.
What eight?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo anupubbaninno anupubbapoṇo anupubbapabbhāro, na āyatakeneva papāto;
segs.e: The ocean gradually slants, slopes, and inclines, with no abrupt precipice.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā, na āyatakeneva aññāpaṭivedho.
segs.e: In the same way in this teaching and training the penetration to enlightenment comes from gradual training, progress, and practice, not abruptly.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā, na āyatakeneva aññāpaṭivedho;
ayaṁ, bhikkhave, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti …pe…
segs.e: This is the first thing the mendicants love about this teaching and training. …

segs.p: seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo mahataṁ bhūtānaṁ āvāso; tatrime bhūtā—timi timiṅgalo timirapiṅgalo asurā nāgā gandhabbā, vasanti mahāsamudde yojanasatikāpi attabhāvā …pe… pañcayojanasatikāpi attabhāvā;
segs.e: Many great beings live in the ocean, such as leviathans, leviathan-gulpers, leviathan-gulper-gulpers, titans, dragons, and centaurs. In the ocean there are life-forms a hundred leagues long, or even two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, or five hundred leagues long.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ayaṁ dhammavinayo mahataṁ bhūtānaṁ āvāso. Tatrime bhūtā—sotāpanno sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno …pe… arahā arahattāya paṭipanno.
segs.e: In the same way, great beings live in this teaching and training, and these are those beings. The stream-enterer and the one practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry. The once-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of once-return. The non-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of non-return. The perfected one, and the one practicing for perfection.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, ayaṁ dhammavinayo mahataṁ bhūtānaṁ āvāso; tatrime bhūtā—sotāpanno sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno …pe… arahā arahattāya paṭipanno;
ayaṁ, bhikkhave, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye aṭṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo, yaṁ disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramanti.
segs.e: This is the eighth thing the mendicants love about this teaching and training.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, ye disvā disvā bhikkhū imasmiṁ dhammavinaye abhiramantī”ti.
segs.e: Seeing these eight incredible and amazing things, the mendicants love this teaching and training.”
Numbered Discourses 8.21
3. Householders
With Ugga of Vesālī

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, acchariyehi abbhutehi dhammehi samannāgataṁ uggaṁ gahapatiṁ vesālikaṁ dhārethā”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, you should remember the householder Ugga of Vesālī as someone who has eight amazing and incredible qualities.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ pāvisi.
segs.e: When he had spoken, the Holy One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena uggassa gahapatino vesālikassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then a certain mendicant robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the householder Ugga of Vesālī, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho uggo gahapati vesāliko yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ bhikkhuṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho uggaṁ gahapatiṁ vesālikaṁ so bhikkhu etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Ugga of Vesālī went up to that mendicant, bowed, and sat down to one side. The mendicant said to him:

segs.p: “Aṭṭhahi kho tvaṁ, gahapati, acchariyehi abbhutehi dhammehi samannāgato bhagavatā byākato.
segs.e: “Householder, the Buddha declared that you have eight amazing and incredible qualities.

segs.p: Katame te, gahapati, aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, yehi tvaṁ samannāgato bhagavatā byākato”ti?
segs.e: What are the eight qualities that he spoke of?”
“Sir, I don’t know

segs.p: ‘katamehi aṭṭhahi acchariyehi abbhutehi dhammehi samannāgato bhagavatā byākato’ti.
segs.e: what eight amazing and incredible qualities the Buddha was referring to.

segs.p: Api ca, bhante, ye me aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā saṁvijjanti,;
segs.e: But these eight amazing and incredible qualities are found in me.

segs.p: taṁ suṇohi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, gahapatī”ti kho so bhikkhu uggassa gahapatino vesālikassa paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, householder,” replied the mendicant.
Ugga of Vesālī said this:
“Sir, when I first saw the Buddha off in the distance,

segs.p: saha dassaneneva me, bhante, bhagavato cittaṁ pasīdi.
segs.e: my heart was inspired as soon as I saw him.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the first incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, bhante, pasannacitto bhagavantaṁ payirupāsiṁ.
segs.e: With confident heart I paid homage to the Buddha.

segs.p: Tassa me bhagavā anupubbiṁ kathaṁ kathesi, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The Buddha taught me step by step,

segs.p: dānakathaṁ sīlakathaṁ saggakathaṁ; kāmānaṁ ādīnavaṁ okāraṁ saṅkilesaṁ, nekkhamme ānisaṁsaṁ pakāsesi.
segs.e: with a talk on giving, ethical conduct, and heaven. He revealed the drawbacks of sensual pleasures, so sordid and corrupt, and the benefit of renunciation.

segs.p: Yadā maṁ bhagavā aññāsi kallacittaṁ muducittaṁ vinīvaraṇacittaṁ udaggacittaṁ pasannacittaṁ, atha yā buddhānaṁ sāmukkaṁsikā dhammadesanā taṁ pakāsesi—
segs.e: And when he knew that my mind was ready, pliable, rid of hindrances, elated, and confident he revealed the special teaching of the Buddhas:
suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṁ vatthaṁ apagatakāḷakaṁ sammadeva rajanaṁ paṭiggaṇheyya;
segs.e: Just as a clean cloth rid of stains would properly absorb dye,

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho me tasmiṁyeva āsane virajaṁ vītamalaṁ dhammacakkhuṁ udapādi:
segs.e: in that very seat the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in me:
‘Everything that is liable to arise is liable to cease.’

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, bhante, diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṅkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane
segs.e: I saw, attained, understood, and fathomed the Dhamma. I went beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, and became self-assured and independent of others regarding the Teacher’s instructions.

segs.p: tattheva buddhañca dhammañca saṅghañca saraṇaṁ agamāsiṁ, brahmacariyapañcamāni ca sikkhāpadāni samādiyiṁ.
segs.e: Right there I went for refuge to the Buddha, his teaching, and the Saṅgha. And I undertook the five training rules with chastity as the fifth.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, dutiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the second incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, catasso komāriyo pajāpatiyo ahesuṁ.
segs.e: I had four teenage wives.

segs.p: Atha khvāhaṁ, bhante, yena tā pajāpatiyo tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā tā pajāpatiyo etadavacaṁ:
segs.e: And I went to them and said:
‘Sisters, I’ve undertaken the five training rules with chastity as fifth.

segs.p: Yā icchati sā idheva bhoge ca bhuñjatu puññāni ca karotu, sakāni vā ñātikulāni gacchatu.
segs.e: If you wish, you may stay here, enjoy my wealth, and do good deeds. Or you can return to your own families.

segs.p: Hoti vā pana purisādhippāyo, kassa vo dammī’ti?
segs.e: Or would you prefer if I gave you to another man?’

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, sā, bhante, jeṭṭhā pajāpati maṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When I said this, my eldest wife said to me:
‘Master, please give me to a man named so-and-so.’

segs.p: Atha kho ahaṁ, bhante, taṁ purisaṁ pakkosāpetvā vāmena hatthena pajāpatiṁ gahetvā dakkhiṇena hatthena bhiṅgāraṁ gahetvā tassa purisassa oṇojesiṁ.
segs.e: Then I summoned that man. Taking my wife with my left hand and a ceremonial vase with my right, I presented her to that man with the pouring of water.

segs.p: Komāriṁ kho panāhaṁ, bhante, dāraṁ pariccajanto nābhijānāmi cittassa aññathattaṁ.
segs.e: But I can’t recall getting upset while giving away my teenage wife.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, tatiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the third incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: Saṁvijjanti kho pana me, bhante, kule bhogā.
segs.e: And though my family has wealth,

segs.p: Te ca kho appaṭivibhattā sīlavantehi kalyāṇadhammehi.
segs.e: it’s shared without reserve with ethical people of good character.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, catuttho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the fourth incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho panāhaṁ, bhante, bhikkhuṁ payirupāsāmi;
segs.e: When I pay homage to a mendicant,
I do so carefully, not carelessly.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, pañcamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the fifth incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: So ce, bhante, me āyasmā dhammaṁ deseti;
segs.e: If that venerable teaches me the Dhamma,
I listen carefully, not carelessly.

segs.p: No ce me so āyasmā dhammaṁ deseti, ahamassa dhammaṁ desemi.
segs.e: But if they don’t teach me the Dhamma, I teach them.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, chaṭṭho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the sixth incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: Anacchariyaṁ kho pana maṁ, bhante, devatā upasaṅkamitvā ārocenti:
segs.e: It’s not unusual for deities to come to me and announce:
‘Householder, the Buddha’s teaching is well explained!’

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, ahaṁ, bhante, tā devatā evaṁ vadāmi:
segs.e: When they say this I say to them:

segs.p: ‘vadeyyātha vā evaṁ kho tumhe devatā no vā vadeyyātha, atha kho svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Buddha’s teaching is well explained, regardless of whether or not you deities say so!’

segs.p: Na kho panāhaṁ, bhante, abhijānāmi tatonidānaṁ cittassa unnatiṁ:
segs.e: But I don’t recall getting too excited by the fact that

segs.p: ‘maṁ vā devatā upasaṅkamanti, ahaṁ vā devatāhi saddhiṁ sallapāmī’ti.
segs.e: the deities come to me, and I have a conversation with them.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, sattamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the seventh incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: Yānimāni, bhante, bhagavatā desitāni pañcorambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni, nāhaṁ tesaṁ kiñci attani appahīnaṁ samanupassāmi.
segs.e: Of the five lower fetters taught by the Buddha, I don’t see any that I haven’t given up.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, aṭṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the eighth incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: Ime kho me, bhante, aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā saṁvijjanti.
segs.e: These eight amazing and incredible qualities are found in me.
But I don’t know

segs.p: katamehi cāhaṁ aṭṭhahi acchariyehi abbhutehi dhammehi samannāgato bhagavatā byākato”ti.
segs.e: what eight amazing and incredible qualities the Buddha was referring to.”

segs.p: Atha kho so bhikkhu uggassa gahapatino vesālikassa nivesane piṇḍapātaṁ gahetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then that mendicant, after taking almsfood in Ugga of Vesālī’s home, rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Atha kho so bhikkhu pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then after the meal, on his return from almsround, he went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu yāvatako ahosi uggena gahapatinā vesālikena saddhiṁ kathāsallāpo, taṁ sabbaṁ bhagavato ārocesi.
segs.e: He informed the Buddha of all he had discussed with the householder Ugga of Vesālī. The Buddha said:
“Good, good, mendicant!

segs.p: Yathā taṁ uggo gahapati vesāliko sammā byākaramāno byākareyya, imeheva kho, bhikkhu, aṭṭhahi acchariyehi abbhutehi dhammehi samannāgato uggo gahapati vesāliko mayā byākato.
segs.e: When I declared that the householder Ugga of Vesālī was someone who has eight amazing and incredible qualities, I was referring to the same eight qualities that he rightly explained to you.

segs.p: Imehi ca pana, bhikkhu, aṭṭhahi acchariyehi abbhutehi dhammehi samannāgataṁ uggaṁ gahapatiṁ vesālikaṁ dhārehī”ti.
segs.e: You should remember the householder Ugga of Vesālī as someone who possesses these eight amazing and incredible qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 8.22
3. Householders
With Uggata of Elephant Village

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vajjīsu viharati hatthigāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Vajjis at Elephant Village.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, acchariyehi abbhutehi dhammehi samannāgataṁ uggaṁ gahapatiṁ hatthigāmakaṁ dhārethā”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, you should remember the householder Uggata of Elephant Village as someone who has eight amazing and incredible qualities.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ pāvisi.
segs.e: When he had spoken, the Holy One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena uggassa gahapatino hatthigāmakassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then a certain mendicant robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the householder Uggata of Elephant Village, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho uggo gahapati hatthigāmako yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ bhikkhuṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho uggaṁ gahapatiṁ hatthigāmakaṁ so bhikkhu etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Uggata of Elephant Village went up to that mendicant, bowed, and sat down to one side. The mendicant said to him:

segs.p: “aṭṭhahi kho tvaṁ, gahapati, acchariyehi abbhutehi dhammehi samannāgato bhagavatā byākato.
segs.e: “Householder, the Buddha declared that you have eight amazing and incredible qualities.

segs.p: Katame te, gahapati, aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā, yehi tvaṁ samannāgato bhagavatā byākato”ti?
segs.e: What are the eight qualities that he spoke of?”
“Sir, I don’t know

segs.p: ‘katamehi aṭṭhahi acchariyehi abbhutehi dhammehi samannāgato bhagavatā byākato’ti.
segs.e: what eight amazing and incredible qualities the Buddha was referring to.

segs.p: Api ca, bhante, ye me aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutā dhammā saṁvijjanti,
segs.e: But these eight amazing and incredible qualities are found in me.

segs.p: taṁ suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, gahapatī”ti kho so bhikkhu uggassa gahapatino hatthigāmakassa paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, householder,” replied the mendicant.
Uggata of Elephant Village said this:

segs.p: “yadāhaṁ, bhante, nāgavane paricaranto bhagavantaṁ paṭhamaṁ dūratova addasaṁ;
segs.e: “Sir, when I first saw the Buddha off in the distance I was partying in the Dragon’s Park.

segs.p: saha dassaneneva me, bhante, bhagavato cittaṁ pasīdi, surāmado ca pahīyi.
segs.e: My heart was inspired as soon as I saw him, and I sobered up.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the first incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, bhante, pasannacitto bhagavantaṁ payirupāsiṁ.
segs.e: With confident heart I paid homage to the Buddha.

segs.p: Tassa me bhagavā anupubbiṁ kathaṁ kathesi, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: The Buddha taught me step by step, with

segs.p: dānakathaṁ sīlakathaṁ saggakathaṁ; kāmānaṁ ādīnavaṁ okāraṁ saṅkilesaṁ, nekkhamme ānisaṁsaṁ pakāsesi.
segs.e: a talk on giving, ethical conduct, and heaven. He revealed the drawbacks of sensual pleasures, so sordid and corrupt, and the benefit of renunciation.

segs.p: Yadā maṁ bhagavā aññāsi kallacittaṁ muducittaṁ vinīvaraṇacittaṁ udaggacittaṁ pasannacittaṁ, atha yā buddhānaṁ sāmukkaṁsikā dhammadesanā taṁ pakāsesi—
segs.e: And when he knew that my mind was ready, pliable, rid of hindrances, elated, and confident he revealed the special teaching of the Buddhas:
suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṁ vatthaṁ apagatakāḷakaṁ sammadeva rajanaṁ paṭiggaṇheyya;
segs.e: Just as a clean cloth rid of stains would properly absorb dye,

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho me tasmiṁyeva āsane virajaṁ vītamalaṁ dhammacakkhuṁ udapādi:
segs.e: in that very seat the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in me:
‘Everything that is liable to arise is liable to cease.’

segs.p: So kho ahaṁ, bhante, diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṅkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane tattheva buddhañca dhammañca saṅghañca saraṇaṁ agamāsiṁ, brahmacariyapañcamāni ca sikkhāpadāni samādiyiṁ.
segs.e: I saw, attained, understood, and fathomed the Dhamma. I went beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, and became self-assured and independent of others regarding the Teacher’s instructions. Right there I went for refuge to the Buddha, his teaching, and the Saṅgha. And I undertook the five training rules with chastity as the fifth.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, dutiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the second incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, catasso komāriyo pajāpatiyo ahesuṁ.
segs.e: I had four teenage wives.

segs.p: Atha khvāhaṁ, bhante, yena tā pajāpatiyo tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā tā pajāpatiyo etadavacaṁ:
segs.e: And I went to them and said:
‘Sisters, I’ve undertaken the five training rules with chastity as fifth.

segs.p: Yā icchati sā idheva bhoge ca bhuñjatu puññāni ca karotu, sakāni vā ñātikulāni gacchatu.
segs.e: If you wish, you may stay here, enjoy my wealth, and do good deeds. Or you can return to your own families.

segs.p: Hoti vā pana purisādhippāyo, kassa vo dammī’ti?
segs.e: Or would you prefer if I gave you to another man?’

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, sā, bhante, jeṭṭhā pajāpati maṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When I said this, my eldest wife said to me:
‘Master, please give me to the man named so-and-so.’

segs.p: Atha kho ahaṁ, bhante, taṁ purisaṁ pakkosāpetvā vāmena hatthena pajāpatiṁ gahetvā dakkhiṇena hatthena bhiṅgāraṁ gahetvā tassa purisassa oṇojesiṁ.
segs.e: Then I summoned that man. Taking my wife with my left hand and a ceremonial vase with my right, I presented her to that man with the pouring of water.

segs.p: Komāriṁ kho panāhaṁ, bhante, dāraṁ pariccajanto nābhijānāmi cittassa aññathattaṁ.
segs.e: But I can’t recall getting upset while giving away my teenage wife.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, tatiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the third incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: Saṁvijjanti kho pana me, bhante, kule bhogā.
segs.e: And though my family has wealth,

segs.p: Te ca kho appaṭivibhattā sīlavantehi kalyāṇadhammehi.
segs.e: it’s shared without reserve with ethical people of good character.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, catuttho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the fourth incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho panāhaṁ, bhante, bhikkhuṁ payirupāsāmi;
segs.e: When I pay homage to a mendicant,
I do so carefully, not carelessly.

segs.p: So ce me āyasmā dhammaṁ deseti;
segs.e: If that venerable teaches me the Dhamma,
I listen carefully, not carelessly.

segs.p: No ce me so āyasmā dhammaṁ deseti, ahamassa dhammaṁ desemi.
segs.e: But if they don’t teach me the Dhamma, I teach them.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, pañcamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo saṁvijjati.
segs.e: This is the fifth incredible and amazing quality found in me.

segs.p: Anacchariyaṁ kho pana, bhante, saṅghe nimantite devatā upasaṅkamitvā ārocenti:
segs.e: It’s not unusual for deities to come to me when the Saṅgha has been invited and announce:

segs.p: ‘asuko, gahapati, bhikkhu ubhatobhāgavimutto asuko paññāvimutto asuko kāyasakkhī asuko diṭṭhippatto asuko saddhāvimutto asuko dhammānusārī asuko saddhānusārī asuko sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo asuko dussīlo pāpadhammo’ti.
segs.e: ‘Householder, that mendicant is freed both ways. That one is freed by wisdom. That one is a direct witness. That one is attained to view. That one is freed by faith.
