segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṁ dānaṁ mahādānaṁ aggaññaṁ rattaññaṁ vaṁsaññaṁ porāṇaṁ asaṅkiṇṇaṁ asaṅkiṇṇapubbaṁ, na saṅkiyati na saṅkiyissati, appaṭikuṭṭhaṁ samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhi.
segs.e: This is the first gift that is a great offering, primordial, long-standing, customary, and traditional. It is uncorrupted, as it has been since the beginning. It’s not being corrupted now nor will it be. Sensible ascetics and brahmins don’t look down on it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro sovaggiko sukhavipāko saggasaṁvattaniko, iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fourth kind of overflowing merit …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple gives up stealing. …
This is the fifth kind of overflowing merit …
Furthermore, a noble disciple gives up sexual misconduct. …
This is the sixth kind of overflowing merit …
Furthermore, a noble disciple gives up lying. …
This is the seventh kind of overflowing merit …
Furthermore, a noble disciple gives up intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako aparimāṇānaṁ sattānaṁ abhayaṁ deti averaṁ deti abyābajjhaṁ deti.
segs.e: By so doing they give to countless sentient beings the gift of freedom from fear, enmity, and ill will.

segs.p: Aparimāṇānaṁ sattānaṁ abhayaṁ datvā averaṁ datvā abyābajjhaṁ datvā, aparimāṇassa abhayassa averassa abyābajjhassa bhāgī hoti.
segs.e: And they themselves also enjoy unlimited freedom from fear, enmity, and ill will.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamaṁ dānaṁ mahādānaṁ aggaññaṁ rattaññaṁ vaṁsaññaṁ porāṇaṁ asaṅkiṇṇaṁ asaṅkiṇṇapubbaṁ, na saṅkiyati na saṅkiyissati, appaṭikuṭṭhaṁ samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhi.
segs.e: This is the fifth gift that is a great offering, primordial, long-standing, customary, and traditional. It is uncorrupted, as it has been since the beginning. It’s not being corrupted now nor will it be. Sensible ascetics and brahmins don’t look down on it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhamo puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro sovaggiko sukhavipāko saggasaṁvattaniko, iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the eighth kind of overflowing merit …

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha puññābhisandā kusalābhisandā sukhassāhārā sovaggikā sukhavipākā saggasaṁvattanikā, iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the eight kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness. They nurture happiness and are conducive to heaven, ripening in happiness and leading to heaven. They lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, to welfare and happiness.”
Numbered Discourses 8.40
4. Giving
The Results of Misconduct

segs.p: “Pāṇātipāto, bhikkhave, āsevito bhāvito bahulīkato nirayasaṁvattaniko tiracchānayonisaṁvattaniko pettivisayasaṁvattaniko.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the killing of living creatures, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Yo sabbalahuso pāṇātipātassa vipāko, manussabhūtassa appāyukasaṁvattaniko hoti.
segs.e: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is a short lifespan.

segs.p: Adinnādānaṁ, bhikkhave, āsevitaṁ bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ nirayasaṁvattanikaṁ tiracchānayonisaṁvattanikaṁ pettivisayasaṁvattanikaṁ.
segs.e: Stealing, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Yo sabbalahuso adinnādānassa vipāko, manussabhūtassa bhogabyasanasaṁvattaniko hoti.
segs.e: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is loss of wealth.

segs.p: Kāmesumicchācāro, bhikkhave, āsevito bhāvito bahulīkato nirayasaṁvattaniko tiracchānayonisaṁvattaniko pettivisayasaṁvattaniko.
segs.e: Sexual misconduct, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Yo sabbalahuso kāmesumicchācārassa vipāko, manussabhūtassa sapattaverasaṁvattaniko hoti.
segs.e: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is rivalry and enmity.

segs.p: Musāvādo, bhikkhave, āsevito bhāvito bahulīkato nirayasaṁvattaniko tiracchānayonisaṁvattaniko pettivisayasaṁvattaniko.
segs.e: Lying, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Yo sabbalahuso musāvādassa vipāko, manussabhūtassa abhūtabbhakkhānasaṁvattaniko hoti.
segs.e: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is false accusations.

segs.p: Pisuṇā, bhikkhave, vācā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkatā nirayasaṁvattanikā tiracchānayonisaṁvattanikā pettivisayasaṁvattanikā.
segs.e: Backbiting, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Yo sabbalahuso pisuṇāya vācāya vipāko, manussabhūtassa mittehi bhedanasaṁvattaniko hoti.
segs.e: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is being divided against friends.

segs.p: Pharusā, bhikkhave, vācā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkatā nirayasaṁvattanikā tiracchānayonisaṁvattanikā pettivisayasaṁvattanikā.
segs.e: Harsh speech, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Yo sabbalahuso pharusāya vācāya vipāko, manussabhūtassa amanāpasaddasaṁvattaniko hoti.
segs.e: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is hearing disagreeable things.

segs.p: Samphappalāpo, bhikkhave, āsevito bhāvito bahulīkato nirayasaṁvattaniko tiracchānayonisaṁvattaniko pettivisayasaṁvattaniko.
segs.e: Talking nonsense, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Yo sabbalahuso samphappalāpassa vipāko, manussabhūtassa anādeyyavācāsaṁvattaniko hoti.
segs.e: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is that no one takes what you say seriously.

segs.p: Surāmerayapānaṁ, bhikkhave, āsevitaṁ bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ nirayasaṁvattanikaṁ tiracchānayonisaṁvattanikaṁ pettivisayasaṁvattanikaṁ.
segs.e: Drinking beer and wine, when cultivated, developed, and practiced, leads to hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Yo sabbalahuso surāmerayapānassa vipāko, manussabhūtassa ummattakasaṁvattaniko hotī”ti.
segs.e: The minimum result it leads to for a human being is madness.”
Numbered Discourses 8.41
5. Sabbath
The Sabbath With Eight Factors, In Brief
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato, bhikkhave, uposatho upavuttho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the observance of the sabbath with its eight factors is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.

segs.p: Kathaṁ upavuttho ca, bhikkhave, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato uposatho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro?
segs.e: And how should it be observed?
It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘yāvajīvaṁ arahanto pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā nihitadaṇḍā nihitasatthā lajjī dayāpannā, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampino viharanti.
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They are scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharāmi.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. I’ll be scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its first factor.

segs.p: ‘Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭiviratā dinnādāyī dinnapāṭikaṅkhī, athenena sucibhūtena attanā viharanti.
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up stealing. They take only what’s given, and expect only what’s given. They keep themselves clean by not thieving.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato dinnādāyī dinnapāṭikaṅkhī, athenena sucibhūtena attanā viharāmi.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up stealing. I’ll take only what’s given, and expect only what’s given. I’ll keep myself clean by not thieving.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its second factor.

segs.p: ‘Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto abrahmacariyaṁ pahāya brahmacārino ārācārino viratā methunā gāmadhammā.
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up unchastity. They are chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ abrahmacariyaṁ pahāya brahmacārī ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up unchastity. I will be chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its third factor.

segs.p: ‘Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto musāvādaṁ pahāya musāvādā paṭiviratā saccavādino saccasandhā thetā paccayikā avisaṁvādako lokassa.
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up lying. They speak the truth and stick to the truth. They’re honest and dependable, and don’t trick the world with their words.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ musāvādaṁ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato saccavādī saccasandho theto paccayiko avisaṁvādako lokassa.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up lying. I’ll speak the truth and stick to the truth. I’ll be honest and dependable, and won’t trick the world with my words.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its fourth factor.
‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṁ pahāya surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its fifth factor.
‘As long as they live, the perfected ones eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night and from food at the wrong time.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ ekabhattiko rattūparato virato vikālabhojanā.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night and food at the wrong time.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its sixth factor.
‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up seeing shows of dancing, singing, and music; and attiring and adorning themselves with garlands, fragrance, and makeup.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ naccagītavāditavisūkadassanamālāgandhavilepanadhāraṇamaṇḍanavibhūsanaṭṭhānaṁ pahāya naccagītavāditavisūkadassanamālāgandhavilepanadhāraṇamaṇḍanavibhūsanaṭṭhānā paṭivirato.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up seeing shows of dancing, singing, and music; and attiring and adorning myself with garlands, fragrance, and makeup.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its seventh factor.

segs.p: ‘Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto uccāsayanamahāsayanaṁ pahāya uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭiviratā nīcaseyyaṁ kappenti—mañcake vā tiṇasanthārake vā.
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up high and luxurious beds. They sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ uccāsayanamahāsayanaṁ pahāya uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭivirato nīcaseyyaṁ kappemi—mañcake vā tiṇasanthārake vā.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up high and luxurious beds. I’ll sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its eighth factor.

segs.p: Evaṁ upavuttho kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato uposatho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro”ti.
segs.e: The observance of the sabbath with its eight factors in this way is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.”
Numbered Discourses 8.42
5. Sabbath
The Sabbath With Eight Factors, In Detail

segs.p: “Aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato, bhikkhave, uposatho upavuttho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the observance of the sabbath with its eight factors is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.

segs.p: Kathaṁ upavuttho ca, bhikkhave, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato uposatho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro?
segs.e: And how should it be observed?
It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘yāvajīvaṁ arahanto pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā nihitadaṇḍā nihitasatthā lajjī dayāpannā, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampino viharanti.
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They are scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharāmi.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. I’ll be scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its first factor. …

segs.p: ‘Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto uccāsayanamahāsayanaṁ pahāya uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭiviratā nīcaseyyaṁ kappenti—mañcake vā tiṇasanthārake vā.
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up high and luxurious beds. They sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ uccāsayanamahāsayanaṁ pahāya uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭivirato nīcaseyyaṁ kappemi—mañcake vā tiṇasanthārake vā.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up high and luxurious beds. I’ll sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its eighth factor.

segs.p: Evaṁ upavuttho kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato uposatho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro.
segs.e: The observance of the sabbath with its eight factors in this way is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.
How much so?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yo imesaṁ soḷasannaṁ mahājanapadānaṁ pahūtarattaratanānaṁ issariyādhipaccaṁ rajjaṁ kāreyya, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: Suppose you were to rule as sovereign lord over these sixteen great countries—Aṅga, Magadha, Kāsi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Cetī, Vaccha, Kuru, Pañcāla, Maccha, Sūrasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhāra, and Persia—full of the seven treasures.

segs.p: aṅgānaṁ magadhānaṁ kāsīnaṁ kosalānaṁ vajjīnaṁ mallānaṁ cetīnaṁ vaṅgānaṁ kurūnaṁ pañcālānaṁ macchānaṁ sūrasenānaṁ assakānaṁ avantīnaṁ gandhārānaṁ kambojānaṁ, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgatassa uposathassa etaṁ kalaṁ nāgghati soḷasiṁ.
segs.e: This wouldn’t be worth a sixteenth part of the sabbath with its eight factors.
Why is that?

segs.p: Kapaṇaṁ, bhikkhave, mānusakaṁ rajjaṁ dibbaṁ sukhaṁ upanidhāya.
segs.e: Because human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.

segs.p: Yāni, bhikkhave, mānusakāni paññāsa vassāni, cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Fifty years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods of the four great kings.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni pañca vassasatāni cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of the four great kings is five hundred of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

segs.p: Yāni, bhikkhave, mānusakāni vassasatāni, tāvatiṁsānaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: A hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods of the thirty-three.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbaṁ vassasahassaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of the thirty-three is a thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā tāvatiṁsānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods of the thirty-three.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

segs.p: Yāni, bhikkhave, mānusakāni dve vassasatāni, yāmānaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Two hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods of Yama.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni dve vassasahassāni yāmānaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of Yama is two thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā yāmānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods of Yama.

‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

segs.p: Yāni, bhikkhave, mānusakāni cattāri vassasatāni, tusitānaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Four hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the joyful gods.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni cattāri vassasahassāni tusitānaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the joyful gods is four thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā tusitānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:

‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

segs.p: Yāni, bhikkhave, mānusakāni aṭṭha vassasatāni, nimmānaratīnaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Eight hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods who love to create.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni aṭṭha vassasahassāni nimmānaratīnaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods who love to create is eight thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā nimmānaratīnaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods who love to create.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

segs.p: Yāni, bhikkhave, mānusakāni soḷasa vassasatāni, paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Sixteen hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods who control what is created by others.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni soḷasa vassasahassāni paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods who control what is created by others is sixteen thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’
You shouldn’t kill living creatures, or steal,

segs.p: Musā na bhāse na ca majjapo siyā;
segs.e: or lie, or drink liquor.
Be chaste, refraining from sex,
and don’t eat at night, the wrong time.

segs.p: Mālaṁ na dhāre na ca gandhamācare,
segs.e: Not wearing garlands or applying fragrance,
you should sleep on a low bed, <j>or a mat on the ground.
This is the eight-factored sabbath, they say,
revealed by the Buddha, <j>who has gone to suffering’s end.

segs.p: Cando ca suriyo ca ubho sudassanā,
segs.e: The moon and sun are both fair to see,
radiating as far as they revolve.
Those dispellers of darkness, travelers in midair,
shine in the firmament, dazzling the quarters.
All of the wealth that’s found in this realm—

segs.p: Tasmā hi nārī ca naro ca sīlavā,
segs.e: So an ethical woman or man,

blameless, they go to a heavenly place.”

5. Sabbath
With Vāseṭṭha on the Sabbath

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho vāseṭṭho upāsako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho vāseṭṭhaṁ upāsakaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the layman Vāseṭṭha went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:
“Vāseṭṭha, the observance of the sabbath with its eight factors is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful …
blameless, they go to a heavenly place.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, vāseṭṭho upāsako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Vāseṭṭha said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “piyā me, bhante, ñātisālohitā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavaseyyuṁ, piyānampi me assa ñātisālohitānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.
segs.e: “If my loved ones—relatives and kin—were to observe this sabbath with its eight factors, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Sabbe cepi, bhante, khattiyā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavaseyyuṁ, sabbesampissa khattiyānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya. Sabbe cepi, bhante, brāhmaṇā …pe… vessā … suddā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavaseyyuṁ, sabbesampissa suddānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.
segs.e: If all the aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, and menials were to observe this sabbath with its eight factors, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.”
“That’s so true, Vāseṭṭha! That’s so true, Vāseṭṭha!

segs.p: Sabbe cepi, vāseṭṭha, khattiyā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavaseyyuṁ, sabbesampissa khattiyānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya. Sabbe cepi, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇā …pe… vessā … suddā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavaseyyuṁ, sabbesampissa suddānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.
segs.e: If all the aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, and menials were to observe this sabbath with its eight factors, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Sadevako cepi, vāseṭṭha, loko samārako sabrahmako sassamaṇabrāhmaṇī pajā sadevamanussā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavaseyyuṁ, sadevakassapissa lokassa samārakassa sabrahmakassa sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.
segs.e: If the whole world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—were to observe this sabbath with its eight factors, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Ime cepi, vāseṭṭha, mahāsālā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavaseyyuṁ, imesampissa mahāsālānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya (…).
segs.e: If these great sal trees were to observe this sabbath with its eight factors, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness—if they were sentient.
How much more then a human being!”
Numbered Discourses 8.45
5. Sabbath
With Bojjhā on the Sabbath

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho bojjhā upāsikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho bojjhaṁ upāsikaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the laywoman Bojjhā went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to her:

segs.p: “Aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato, bojjhe, uposatho upavuttho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro.
segs.e: “Bojjhā, the observance of the sabbath with its eight factors is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.

segs.p: Kathaṁ upavuttho ca, bojjhe, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato uposatho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro?
segs.e: And how should it be observed?
It’s when a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘yāvajīvaṁ arahanto pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā nihitadaṇḍā nihitasatthā lajjī dayāpannā sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampino viharanti.
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They are scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharāmi.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. I’ll be scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its first factor. …

segs.p: ‘Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto uccāsayanamahāsayanaṁ pahāya uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭiviratā nīcaseyyaṁ kappenti—mañcake vā tiṇasanthārake vā.
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up high and luxurious beds. They sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

segs.p: Ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ uccāsayanamahāsayanaṁ pahāya uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭivirato nīcaseyyaṁ kappemi—mañcake vā tiṇasanthārake vā.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up high and luxurious beds. I’ll sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

segs.p: Imināpaṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
This is its eighth factor.

segs.p: Evaṁ upavuttho kho, bojjhe, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato uposatho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro.
segs.e: The observance of the sabbath with its eight factors in this way is very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.
How much so?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bojjhe, yo imesaṁ soḷasannaṁ mahājanapadānaṁ pahūtarattaratanānaṁ issariyādhipaccaṁ rajjaṁ kāreyya, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: Suppose you were to rule as sovereign lord over these sixteen great countries—Aṅga, Magadha, Kāsi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Cetī, Vaccha, Kuru, Pañcāla, Maccha, Sūrasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhāra, and Persia—full of the seven treasures.

segs.p: aṅgānaṁ magadhānaṁ kāsīnaṁ kosalānaṁ vajjīnaṁ mallānaṁ cetīnaṁ vaṅgānaṁ kurūnaṁ pañcālānaṁ macchānaṁ sūrasenānaṁ assakānaṁ avantīnaṁ gandhārānaṁ kambojānaṁ, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgatassa uposathassa etaṁ kalaṁ nāgghati soḷasiṁ.
segs.e: This wouldn’t be worth a sixteenth part of the sabbath with its eight factors.
Why is that?

segs.p: Kapaṇaṁ, bojjhe, mānusakaṁ rajjaṁ dibbaṁ sukhaṁ upanidhāya.
segs.e: Because human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.

segs.p: Yāni, bojjhe, mānusakāni paññāsa vassāni, cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Fifty years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods of the four great kings.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni pañca vassasatāni cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of the four great kings is five hundred of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, bojjhe, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, bojjhe, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’
A hundred years in the human realm …
Two hundred years in the human realm …
Four hundred years in the human realm …
Eight hundred years in the human realm …

segs.p: soḷasa vassasatāni paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Sixteen hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods who control what is created by others.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni soḷasa vassasahassāni paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The life span of the gods who control what is created by others is sixteen thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, bojjhe, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods who control what is created by others.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, bojjhe, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’
You shouldn’t kill living creatures, or steal,

segs.p: Musā na bhāse na ca majjapo siyā;
segs.e: or lie, or drink liquor.
Be chaste, refraining from sex,
and don’t eat at night, the wrong time.

segs.p: Mālaṁ na dhāre na ca gandhamācare,
segs.e: Not wearing garlands or applying fragrance,
you should sleep on a low bed, <j>or a mat on the ground.
This is the eight-factored sabbath, they say,
revealed by the Buddha, <j>who has gone to suffering’s end.

segs.p: Cando ca suriyo ca ubho sudassanā,
segs.e: The moon and sun are both fair to see,
radiating as far as they revolve.
Those dispellers of darkness, travelers in midair,
shine in the firmament, dazzling the quarters.
All of the wealth that’s found in this realm—
pearls, gems, fine beryl too,
mountain gold or lustrous gold,
or the native gold called ‘coruscant’—
they’re not worth a sixteenth part
of the mind developed with love,
as starlight cannot rival the moon.

segs.p: Tasmā hi nārī ca naro ca sīlavā,
segs.e: So an ethical woman or man,
who has observed the eight-factored sabbath,
having made merit whose outcome is happiness,
blameless, they go to a heavenly place.”
Numbered Discourses 8.46
5. Sabbath
Anuruddha and the Agreeable Deities

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā anuruddho divāvihāraṁ gato hoti paṭisallīno.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Anuruddha had gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā manāpakāyikā devatā yenāyasmā anuruddho tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ anuruddhaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho tā devatā āyasmantaṁ anuruddhaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several deities of the Agreeable Host went up to Venerable Anuruddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “mayaṁ, bhante anuruddha, manāpakāyikā nāma devatā tīsu ṭhānesu issariyaṁ kārema vasaṁ vattema.
segs.e: “Honorable Anuruddha, we are the deities called ‘Agreeable’. We wield authority and control over three things.
segs.s: several deities of the Agreeable Host

segs.p: Mayaṁ, bhante anuruddha, yādisakaṁ vaṇṇaṁ ākaṅkhāma tādisakaṁ vaṇṇaṁ ṭhānaso paṭilabhāma;
segs.e: We can turn any color we want on the spot.
segs.s: several deities of the Agreeable Host

segs.p: yādisakaṁ saraṁ ākaṅkhāma tādisakaṁ saraṁ ṭhānaso paṭilabhāma;
segs.e: We can get any voice that we want on the spot.
segs.s: several deities of the Agreeable Host

segs.p: yādisakaṁ sukhaṁ ākaṅkhāma tādisakaṁ sukhaṁ ṭhānaso paṭilabhāma.
segs.e: We can get any pleasure that we want on the spot.
segs.s: several deities of the Agreeable Host

segs.p: Mayaṁ, bhante anuruddha, manāpakāyikā nāma devatā imesu tīsu ṭhānesu issariyaṁ kārema vasaṁ vattemā”ti.
segs.e: We are the deities called ‘Agreeable’. We wield authority and control over these three things.”
segs.s: several deities of the Agreeable Host

segs.e: Then Venerable Anuruddha thought,

segs.p: “aho vatimā devatā sabbāva nīlā assu nīlavaṇṇā nīlavatthā nīlālaṅkārā”ti.
segs.e: “If only these deities would all turn blue, of blue color, clad in blue, adorned with blue!”

segs.p: Atha kho tā devatā āyasmato anuruddhassa cittamaññāya sabbāva nīlā ahesuṁ nīlavaṇṇā nīlavatthā nīlālaṅkārā.
segs.e: Then those deities, knowing Anuruddha’s thought, all turned blue.
Then Venerable Anuruddha thought,
“If only these deities would all turn yellow …”
“If only these gods would all turn red …”

segs.p: sabbāva odātā assu odātavaṇṇā odātavatthā odātālaṅkārā”ti.
segs.e: “If only these gods would all turn white …”

segs.p: Atha kho tā devatā āyasmato anuruddhassa cittamaññāya sabbāva odātā ahesuṁ odātavaṇṇā odātavatthā odātālaṅkārā.
segs.e: Then those deities, knowing Anuruddha’s thought, all turned white.

segs.p: Atha kho tā devatā ekā ca gāyi ekā ca nacci ekā ca accharaṁ vādesi.
segs.e: Then one of those deities sang, one danced, and one snapped her fingers.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma pañcaṅgikassa tūriyassa suvinītassa suppaṭipatāḷitassa kusalehi susamannāhatassa saddo hoti vaggu ca rajanīyo ca kamanīyo ca pemanīyo ca madanīyo ca;
segs.e: Suppose there was a quintet made up of skilled musicians who had practiced well and kept excellent rhythm. They’d sound graceful, tantalizing, sensuous, endearing, and intoxicating.

segs.p: evamevaṁ tāsaṁ devatānaṁ alaṅkārānaṁ saddo hoti vaggu ca rajanīyo ca kamanīyo ca pemanīyo ca madanīyo ca.
segs.e: In the same way the performance by those deities sounded graceful, tantalizing, sensuous, endearing, and intoxicating.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho indriyāni okkhipi.
segs.e: But Venerable Anuruddha averted his senses.

segs.p: Atha kho tā devatā “na khvayyo anuruddho sādiyatī”ti tatthevantaradhāyiṁsu.
segs.e: Then those deities, thinking “Master Anuruddha isn’t enjoying this,” vanished right there.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā anuruddho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, Anuruddha came out of retreat and went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened, adding:

segs.p: Atha kho, bhante, sambahulā manāpakāyikā devatā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, bhante, tā devatā maṁ etadavocuṁ:
‘mayaṁ, bhante anuruddha, manāpakāyikā nāma devatā tīsu ṭhānesu issariyaṁ kārema vasaṁ vattema.
Mayaṁ, bhante anuruddha, yādisakaṁ vaṇṇaṁ ākaṅkhāma tādisakaṁ vaṇṇaṁ ṭhānaso paṭilabhāma;
yādisakaṁ saraṁ ākaṅkhāma tādisakaṁ saraṁ ṭhānaso paṭilabhāma;
yādisakaṁ sukhaṁ ākaṅkhāma tādisakaṁ sukhaṁ ṭhānaso paṭilabhāma.
Mayaṁ, bhante anuruddha, manāpakāyikā nāma devatā imesu tīsu ṭhānesu issariyaṁ kārema vasaṁ vattemā’ti.
‘aho vatimā devatā sabbāva nīlā assu nīlavaṇṇā nīlavatthā nīlālaṅkārā’ti.
Atha kho, bhante, tā devatā mama cittamaññāya sabbāva nīlā ahesuṁ nīlavaṇṇā nīlavatthā nīlālaṅkārā.
sabbāva odātā assu odātavaṇṇā odātavatthā odātālaṅkārā’ti.
Atha kho, bhante, tā devatā mama cittamaññāya sabbāva odātā ahesuṁ odātavaṇṇā odātavatthā odātālaṅkārā.
Atha kho, bhante, tā devatā ekā ca gāyi ekā ca nacci ekā ca accharaṁ vādesi.
Seyyathāpi nāma pañcaṅgikassa tūriyassa suvinītassa suppaṭipatāḷitassa kusalehi susamannāhatassa saddo hoti vaggu ca rajanīyo ca kamanīyo ca pemanīyo ca madanīyo ca;
evamevaṁ tāsaṁ devatānaṁ alaṅkārānaṁ saddo hoti vaggu ca rajanīyo ca kamanīyo ca pemanīyo ca madanīyo ca.
Atha kho, bhante, tā devatā ‘na khvayyo anuruddho sādiyatī’ti tatthevantaradhāyiṁsu.
Katihi nu kho, bhante, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā manāpakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti?
segs.e: “How many qualities do ladies have so that—when their body breaks up, after death—they are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host?”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhahi kho, anuruddha, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā manāpakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: “Anuruddha, when they have eight qualities ladies—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host.
What eight?

segs.p: Idha, anuruddha, mātugāmo yassa mātāpitaro bhattuno denti atthakāmā hitesino anukampakā anukampaṁ upādāya tassa hoti pubbuṭṭhāyinī pacchānipātinī kiṅkārapaṭissāvinī manāpacārinī piyavādinī.
segs.e: Take the case of a lady whose mother and father give her to a husband wanting what’s best for her, out of kindness and sympathy. She would get up before him and go to bed after him, and be obliging, behaving nicely and speaking politely.
She honors, respects, esteems, and venerates those her husband respects, such as

segs.p: mātāti vā pitāti vā samaṇabrāhmaṇāti vā—
segs.e: mother and father, and ascetics and brahmins.

segs.p: te sakkaroti, garuṁ karoti, māneti, pūjeti, abbhāgate ca āsanodakena paṭipūjeti.
segs.e: And when they arrive she serves them with a seat and water.

segs.p: Ye te bhattu abbhantarā kammantā—uṇṇāti vā kappāsāti vā—tattha dakkhā hoti analasā tatrupāyāya vīmaṁsāya samannāgatā alaṁ kātuṁ alaṁ saṁvidhātuṁ.
segs.e: She’s deft and tireless in her husband’s household duties, such as knitting and sewing. She understands how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

segs.p: Yo so bhattu abbhantaro antojano—dāsāti vā pessāti vā kammakarāti vā—
segs.e: She knows what work her husband’s domestic bondservants, servants, and workers have completed, and what they’ve left incomplete.

segs.p: tesaṁ katañca katato jānāti akatañca akatato jānāti, gilānakānañca balābalaṁ jānāti khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyañcassa paccaṁsena saṁvibhajati.
segs.e: She knows who is sick, and who is fit or unwell. She distributes to each a fair portion of fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Yaṁ bhattu āharati dhanaṁ vā dhaññaṁ vā jātarūpaṁ vā taṁ ārakkhena guttiyā sampādeti, tattha ca hoti adhuttī athenī asoṇḍī avināsikā.
segs.e: She ensures that any income her husband earns is guarded and protected, whether money, grain, silver, or gold. She doesn’t overspend, steal, waste, or lose it.

segs.p: Upāsikā kho pana hoti buddhaṁ saraṇaṁ gatā dhammaṁ saraṇaṁ gatā saṅghaṁ saraṇaṁ gatā.
segs.e: She’s a lay follower who has gone for refuge to the Buddha, his teaching, and the Saṅgha.
She’s ethical.

segs.p: pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā, adinnādānā paṭiviratā, kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā, musāvādā paṭiviratā, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā.
segs.e: She doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.
She’s generous.

segs.p: Vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgā payatapāṇinī vossaggaratā yācayogā dānasaṁvibhāgaratā.
segs.e: She lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

segs.p: Imehi kho, anuruddha, aṭṭhahi dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā manāpakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatīti.
segs.e: When they possess these eight qualities ladies—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host.
She’d never look down on her husband,
who’s always eager to work hard,
always looking after her,
and bringing whatever she wants.
And a good woman never scolds her husband
with jealous words.
Being astute, she reveres
those respected by her husband.
She gets up early, works tirelessly,
and manages the domestic help.
She’s agreeable to her husband,
and preserves his wealth.
A lady who fulfills these duties
according to her husband’s desire,
is reborn among the gods
called ‘Agreeable’.”
Numbered Discourses 8.47
5. Sabbath
With Visākhā on the Agreeable Gods

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.
Then Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

segs.p: ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho visākhaṁ migāramātaraṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to her:

segs.p: “Aṭṭhahi kho, visākhe, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā manāpakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: “Visākhā, when they have eight qualities ladies—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host.
What eight?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, mātugāmo yassa mātāpitaro bhattuno denti atthakāmā hitesino anukampakā anukampaṁ upādāya tassa hoti pubbuṭṭhāyinī pacchānipātinī kiṅkārapaṭissāvinī manāpacārinī piyavādinī …pe….
segs.e: Take the case of a lady whose mother and father give her to a husband wanting what’s best for her, out of kindness and sympathy. She would get up before him and go to bed after him, and be obliging, behaving nicely and speaking politely. …
She’s generous.

segs.p: Vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgā payatapāṇinī vossaggaratā yācayogā dānasaṁvibhāgaratā.
segs.e: She lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

segs.p: Imehi kho, visākhe, aṭṭhahi dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā manāpakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatīti.
segs.e: When they possess these eight qualities ladies—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host.
She’d never look down on her husband,
who’s always eager to work hard,
always looking after her,
and bringing whatever she wants.
And a good woman never scolds her husband
with jealous words.
Being astute, she reveres
those respected by her husband.
She gets up early, works tirelessly,
and manages the domestic help.
She’s agreeable to her husband,
and preserves his wealth.
A lady who fulfills these duties
according to her husband’s desire,
is reborn among the gods
called ‘Agreeable’.”
Numbered Discourses 8.48
5. Sabbath
With Nakula’s Mother on the Agreeable Gods

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow, in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood.

segs.p: Atha kho nakulamātā gahapatānī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā …pe…. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho nakulamātaraṁ gahapatāniṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the housewife Nakula’s mother went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to her:

segs.p: “Aṭṭhahi kho, nakulamāte, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā manāpakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: “Nakula’s mother, when they have eight qualities ladies—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host.
What eight?

segs.p: Idha, nakulamāte, mātugāmo yassa mātāpitaro bhattuno denti atthakāmā hitesino anukampakā anukampaṁ upādāya tassa hoti pubbuṭṭhāyinī pacchānipātinī kiṅkārapaṭissāvinī manāpacārinī piyavādinī.
segs.e: Take the case of a lady whose mother and father give her to a husband wanting what’s best for her, out of kindness and sympathy. She would get up before him and go to bed after him, and be obliging, behaving nicely and speaking politely.
She honors, respects, esteems, and venerates those her husband respects, such as

segs.p: mātāti vā pitāti vā samaṇabrāhmaṇāti vā—
segs.e: mother and father, and ascetics and brahmins.

segs.p: te sakkaroti garuṁ karoti māneti pūjeti, abbhāgate ca āsanodakena paṭipūjeti.
segs.e: And when they arrive she serves them with a seat and water.

segs.p: Ye te bhattu abbhantarā kammantā—uṇṇāti vā kappāsāti vā—tattha dakkhā hoti analasā tatrupāyāya vīmaṁsāya samannāgatā alaṁ kātuṁ alaṁ saṁvidhātuṁ.
segs.e: She’s deft and tireless in her husband’s household duties, such as knitting and sewing. She understands how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

segs.p: Yo so bhattu abbhantaro antojano—dāsāti vā pessāti vā kammakarāti vā—
segs.e: She knows what work her husband’s domestic bondservants, servants, and workers have completed, and what they’ve left incomplete.

segs.p: tesaṁ katañca katato jānāti akatañca akatato jānāti, gilānakānañca balābalaṁ jānāti khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyañcassa paccaṁsena saṁvibhajati.
segs.e: She knows who is sick, and who is fit or unwell. She distributes to each a fair portion of fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Yaṁ bhattā āharati dhanaṁ vā dhaññaṁ vā rajataṁ vā jātarūpaṁ vā taṁ ārakkhena guttiyā sampādeti, tattha ca hoti adhuttī athenī asoṇḍī avināsikā.
segs.e: She ensures that any income her husband earns is guarded and protected, whether money, grain, silver, or gold. She doesn’t overspend, steal, waste, or lose it.

segs.p: Upāsikā kho pana hoti buddhaṁ saraṇaṁ gatā dhammaṁ saraṇaṁ gatā saṅghaṁ saraṇaṁ gatā.
segs.e: She’s a lay follower who has gone for refuge to the Buddha, his teaching, and the Saṅgha.
She’s ethical.
She doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Cāgavatī kho pana hoti vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgā payatapāṇinī vossaggaratā yācayogā dānasaṁvibhāgaratā.
segs.e: She’s generous. She lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

segs.p: Imehi kho, nakulamāte, aṭṭhahi dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā manāpakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatīti.
segs.e: When they possess these eight qualities ladies—when their body breaks up, after death—are reborn in company with the Gods of the Agreeable Host.
She’d never look down on her husband,
who’s always eager to work hard,
always looking after her,
and bringing whatever she wants.
And a good woman never scolds her husband
with jealous words.
Being astute, she reveres
those respected by her husband.
She gets up early, works tirelessly,
and manages the domestic help.
She’s agreeable to her husband,
and preserves his wealth.
A lady who fulfills these duties
according to her husband’s desire,
is reborn among the gods
called ‘Agreeable’.”
Numbered Discourses 8.49
5. Sabbath
Winning in This Life (1st)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho visākhā migāramātā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe….
segs.e: Then Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho visākhaṁ migāramātaraṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to her:

segs.p: “Catūhi kho, visākhe, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo idhalokavijayāya paṭipanno hoti, ayaṁsa loko āraddho hoti.
segs.e: “Visākhā, a lady who has four qualities is practicing to win in this life, and she succeeds at it.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, mātugāmo susaṁvihitakammanto hoti, saṅgahitaparijano, bhattu manāpaṁ carati, sambhataṁ anurakkhati.
segs.e: It’s when a lady is well-organized at work, manages the domestic help, acts lovingly toward her husband, and preserves his earnings.
And how is a lady well-organized at work?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, mātugāmo ye te bhattu abbhantarā kammantā—uṇṇāti vā kappāsāti vā—tattha dakkhā hoti analasā tatrupāyāya vīmaṁsāya samannāgatā alaṁ kātuṁ alaṁ saṁvidhātuṁ.
segs.e: It’s when she’s deft and tireless in doing domestic duties for her husband, such as knitting and sewing. She understands how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, mātugāmo susaṁvihitakammanto hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a lady is well-organized at work.
And how does a lady manage the domestic help?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, mātugāmo yo so bhattu abbhantaro antojano—dāsāti vā pessāti vā kammakarāti vā—
segs.e: It’s when she knows what work her husband’s domestic bondservants, servants, and workers have completed, and what they’ve left incomplete.

segs.p: tesaṁ katañca katato jānāti akatañca akatato jānāti, gilānakānañca balābalaṁ jānāti khādanīyaṁ bhojanīyañcassa paccaṁsena saṁvibhajati.
segs.e: She knows who is sick, and who is fit or unwell. She distributes to each a fair portion of fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, mātugāmo saṅgahitaparijano hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a lady manages the domestic help.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, mātugāmo bhattu manāpaṁ carati?
segs.e: And how does a lady act lovingly toward her husband?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, mātugāmo yaṁ bhattu amanāpasaṅkhātaṁ taṁ jīvitahetupi na ajjhācarati.
segs.e: It’s when a lady would not transgress in any way that her husband would not consider agreeable, even for the sake of her own life.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, mātugāmo bhattu manāpaṁ carati.
segs.e: That’s how a lady acts lovingly toward her husband.
And how does a lady preserve his earnings?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, mātugāmo yaṁ bhattā āharati dhanaṁ vā dhaññaṁ vā rajataṁ vā jātarūpaṁ vā taṁ ārakkhena guttiyā sampādeti, tattha ca hoti adhuttī athenī asoṇḍī avināsikā.
segs.e: It’s when she ensures that any income her husband earns is guarded and protected, whether money, grain, silver, or gold. She doesn’t overspend, steal, waste, or lose it.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, mātugāmo sambhataṁ anurakkhati.
segs.e: That’s how a lady preserves his earnings.

segs.p: Imehi kho, visākhe, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo idhalokavijayāya paṭipanno hoti, ayaṁsa loko āraddho hoti.
segs.e: A lady who possesses these four qualities is practicing to win in this life, and she succeeds at it.

segs.p: Catūhi kho, visākhe, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo paralokavijayāya paṭipanno hoti, paraloko āraddho hoti.
segs.e: A lady who has four qualities is practicing to win in the next life, and she succeeds at it.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, mātugāmo saddhāsampanno hoti, sīlasampanno hoti, cāgasampanno hoti, paññāsampanno hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a lady is accomplished in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom.
And how is a lady accomplished in faith?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, mātugāmo saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ:
segs.e: It’s when a lady has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, mātugāmo saddhāsampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a lady is accomplished in faith.
And how is a lady accomplished in ethics?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, mātugāmo pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a lady doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, mātugāmo sīlasampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a lady is accomplished in ethics.
And how is a lady accomplished in generosity?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, mātugāmo vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgā payatapāṇinī vossaggaratā yācayogā dānasaṁvibhāgaratā.
segs.e: It’s when she lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, mātugāmo cāgasampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a lady is accomplished in generosity.
And how is a lady accomplished in wisdom?
It’s when a lady is wise. She has the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

segs.p: evaṁ kho, visākhe, mātugāmo paññāsampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a lady is accomplished in wisdom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, visākhe, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo paralokavijayāya paṭipanno hoti, paraloko āraddho hotīti.
segs.e: A lady who possesses these four qualities is practicing to win in the next life, and she succeeds at it.
She’s organized at work,
and manages the domestic help.
She’s agreeable to her husband,
and preserves his wealth.
Faithful, accomplished in ethics,
bountiful, rid of stinginess,
she always purifies the path
to well-being in lives to come.
And so, a lady in whom
these eight qualities are found
is known as virtuous,
firmly principled, and truthful.
Accomplished in sixteen respects,
complete with the eight factors,
a virtuous laywoman such as she
is reborn in the realm of the Agreeable Gods.”
Numbered Discourses 8.50
