Numbered Discourses 8.51
6. Gotamī
With Gotamī

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho mahāpajāpatī gotamī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho mahāpajāpatī gotamī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahāpajāpati Gotamī went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, please let ladies gain the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”
“Enough, Gotamī.

segs.p: Mā te rucci mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjā”ti.
segs.e: Don’t endorse the going forth for ladies from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho mahāpajāpatī gotamī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time …

segs.p: “sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan”ti.
Mā te rucci mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjā”ti.
Tatiyampi kho mahāpajāpatī gotamī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time, Mahāpajāpati Gotamī said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, please let ladies gain the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”
“Enough, Gotamī.

segs.p: Mā te rucci mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjā”ti.
segs.e: Don’t endorse the going forth for ladies from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

segs.p: Atha kho mahāpajāpatī gotamī “na bhagavā anujānāti mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan”ti dukkhī dummanā assumukhī rudamānā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then Mahāpajāpati Gotamī thought, “The Buddha does not permit ladies to go forth.” Miserable and sad, weeping, with a tearful face, she bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on her right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā kapilavatthusmiṁ yathābhirantaṁ viharitvā yena vesālī tena cārikaṁ pakkāmi.
segs.e: When the Buddha had stayed in Kapilavatthu as long as he pleased, he set out for Vesālī.

segs.p: Anupubbena cārikaṁ caramāno yena vesālī tadavasari.
segs.e: Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Vesālī,

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: where he stayed at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho mahāpajāpatī gotamī kese chedāpetvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā sambahulāhi sākiyānīhi saddhiṁ yena vesālī tena pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then Mahāpajāpati Gotamī had her hair shaved, and dressed in ocher robes. Together with several Sakyan ladies she set out for Vesālī.

segs.p: Anupubbena yena vesālī mahāvanaṁ kūṭāgārasālā tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Traveling stage by stage, she arrived at Vesālī and went to the Great Wood, the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho mahāpajāpatī gotamī sūnehi pādehi rajokiṇṇena gattena dukkhī dummanā assumukhī rudamānā bahidvārakoṭṭhake aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then Mahāpajāpati Gotamī stood crying outside the gate, her feet swollen, her limbs covered with dust, miserable and sad, with tearful face.

segs.p: Addasā kho āyasmā ānando mahāpajāpatiṁ gotamiṁ sūnehi pādehi rajokiṇṇena gattena dukkhiṁ dummanaṁ assumukhiṁ rudamānaṁ bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhitaṁ.
segs.e: Venerable Ānanda saw her standing there,
and said to her,

segs.p: “kiṁ nu tvaṁ, gotami, sūnehi pādehi rajokiṇṇena gattena dukkhī dummanā assumukhī rudamānā bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhitā”ti?
segs.e: “Gotamī, why do you stand crying outside the gate, your feet swollen, your limbs covered with dust, miserable and sad, with tearful face?”

segs.p: “Tathā hi pana, bhante ānanda, na bhagavā anujānāti mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan”ti.
segs.e: “Honorable Ānanda, it’s because the Buddha does not permit ladies to go forth in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

segs.p: “Tena hi tvaṁ, gotami, muhuttaṁ idheva tāva hohi, yāvāhaṁ bhagavantaṁ yācāmi mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, Gotamī, wait here an hour while I ask the Buddha to grant the going forth for ladies.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “esā, bhante, mahāpajāpatī gotamī sūnehi pādehi rajokiṇṇena gattena dukkhī dummanā assumukhī rudamānā bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhitā:
segs.e: “Sir, Mahāpajāpati Gotamī is standing crying outside the gate, her feet swollen, her limbs covered with dust, miserable and sad, with tearful face.

segs.p: ‘na bhagavā anujānāti mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan’ti.
segs.e: She says that it’s because the Buddha does not permit ladies to go forth.

segs.p: Sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan”ti.
segs.e: Sir, please let ladies gain the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”
“Enough, Ānanda.

segs.p: Mā te rucci mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjā”ti.
segs.e: Don’t endorse the going forth for ladies from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”
For a second time …

segs.p: tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time, Ānanda said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, please let ladies gain the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”
“Enough, Ānanda.

segs.p: Mā te rucci mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjā”ti.
segs.e: Don’t endorse the going forth for ladies from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”
Then Venerable Ānanda thought,

segs.p: “na bhagavā anujānāti mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjaṁ.
segs.e: “The Buddha does not permit ladies to go forth.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ aññenapi pariyāyena bhagavantaṁ yāceyyaṁ mātugāmassa tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I try another approach?”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “bhabbo nu kho, bhante, mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitvā sotāpattiphalaṁ vā sakadāgāmiphalaṁ vā anāgāmiphalaṁ vā arahattaphalaṁ vā sacchikātun”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, is a lady able to realize the fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection once she has gone forth?”

segs.p: “Bhabbo, ānanda, mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitvā sotāpattiphalampi sakadāgāmiphalampi anāgāmiphalampi arahattaphalampi sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: “She is able, Ānanda.”

segs.p: “Sace, bhante, bhabbo mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitvā sotāpattiphalampi …pe… arahattaphalampi sacchikātuṁ;
segs.e: “If a lady is able to realize the fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection once she has gone forth.

segs.p: bahukārā, bhante, mahāpajāpatī gotamī bhagavato mātucchā āpādikā posikā khīrassa dāyikā;
segs.e: Sir, Mahāpajāpati has been very helpful to the Buddha. As his aunt, she raised him, nurtured him, and gave him her milk.
When the Buddha’s birth mother passed away, she nurtured him at her own breast.

segs.p: Sādhu, bhante, labheyya mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjan”ti.
segs.e: Sir, please let ladies gain the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One.”

segs.p: “Sace, ānanda, mahāpajāpatī gotamī aṭṭha garudhamme paṭiggaṇhāti, sāvassā hotu upasampadā—
segs.e: “Ānanda, if Mahāpajāpati Gotamī accepts these eight principles of respect, that will be her ordination.

segs.p: Vassasatūpasampannāya bhikkhuniyā tadahūpasampannassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṁ paccuṭṭhānaṁ añjalikammaṁ sāmīcikammaṁ kattabbaṁ.
segs.e: A nun, even if she has been ordained for a hundred years, should bow down to a monk who was ordained that very day. She should rise up for him, greet him with cupped palms, and observe proper etiquette toward him.

segs.p: Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyo.
segs.e: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

segs.p: Na bhikkhuniyā abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṁ upagantabbaṁ.
segs.e: A nun should not commence the rainy season residence in a monastery without monks.

segs.p: Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyo.
segs.e: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

segs.p: Anvaḍḍhamāsaṁ bhikkhuniyā bhikkhusaṅghato dve dhammā paccāsīsitabbā—
segs.e: Each fortnight the nuns should expect two things from the community of monks:
the date of the sabbath, and visiting for advice.

segs.p: Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyo.
segs.e: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

segs.p: Vassaṁvuṭṭhāya bhikkhuniyā ubhatosaṅghe tīhi ṭhānehi pavāretabbaṁ—
segs.e: After completing the rainy season residence the nuns should invite admonition from the communities of both monks and nuns in regard to anything that was

segs.p: diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā.
segs.e: seen, heard, or suspected.

segs.p: Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyo.
segs.e: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

segs.p: Garudhammaṁ ajjhāpannāya bhikkhuniyā ubhatosaṅghe pakkhamānattaṁ caritabbaṁ.
segs.e: A nun who has committed a grave offense should undergo penance in the communities of both monks and nuns for a fortnight.

segs.p: Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyo.
segs.e: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

segs.p: Dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhāya sikkhamānāya ubhatosaṅghe upasampadā pariyesitabbā.
segs.e: A trainee nun who has trained in the six rules for two years should seek ordination from the communities of both monks and nuns.

segs.p: Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyo.
segs.e: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

segs.p: Na kenaci pariyāyena bhikkhuniyā bhikkhu akkositabbo paribhāsitabbo.
segs.e: A nun should not abuse or insult a monk in any way.

segs.p: Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyo.
segs.e: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

segs.p: Ajjatagge ovaṭo bhikkhunīnaṁ bhikkhūsu vacanapatho, anovaṭo bhikkhūnaṁ bhikkhunīsu vacanapatho.
segs.e: From this day forth it is forbidden for nuns to criticize monks, but it is not forbidden for monks to criticize nuns.

segs.p: Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyo.
segs.e: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

segs.p: Sace, ānanda, mahāpajāpatī gotamī ime aṭṭha garudhamme paṭiggaṇhāti, sāvassā hotu upasampadā”ti.
segs.e: If Mahāpajāpati Gotamī accepts these eight principles of respect, that will be her ordination.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato santike ime aṭṭha garudhamme uggahetvā yena mahāpajāpatī gotamī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mahāpajāpatiṁ gotamiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Ānanda, having learned these eight principles of respect from the Buddha himself, went to Mahāpajāpati Gotamī and said:

segs.p: “Sace kho tvaṁ, gotami, aṭṭha garudhamme paṭiggaṇheyyāsi, sāva te bhavissati upasampadā—
segs.e: “Gotamī, if you accept eight principles of respect, that will be your ordination.

segs.p: Vassasatūpasampannāya bhikkhuniyā tadahūpasampannassa bhikkhuno abhivādanaṁ paccuṭṭhānaṁ añjalikammaṁ sāmīcikammaṁ kattabbaṁ.
segs.e: A nun, even if she has been ordained for a hundred years, should bow down to a monk who was ordained that very day. She should rise up for him, greet him with cupped palms, and observe proper etiquette toward him.

segs.p: Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyo …pe….
segs.e: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts. …

segs.p: Ajjatagge ovaṭo bhikkhunīnaṁ bhikkhūsu vacanapatho, anovaṭo bhikkhūnaṁ bhikkhunīsu vacanapatho.
segs.e: From this day forth it is forbidden for nuns to criticize monks, but it is not forbidden for monks to criticize nuns.

segs.p: Ayampi dhammo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā mānetvā pūjetvā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyo.
segs.e: This principle should be honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated, and not transgressed so long as life lasts.

segs.p: Sace kho tvaṁ, gotami, ime aṭṭha garudhamme paṭiggaṇheyyāsi, sāva te bhavissati upasampadā”ti.
segs.e: If you accept these eight principles of respect, that will be your ordination.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhante ānanda, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko sīsaṁnhāto uppalamālaṁ vā vassikamālaṁ vā adhimuttakamālaṁ vā labhitvā ubhohi hatthehi paṭiggahetvā uttamaṅge sirasmiṁ patiṭṭhāpeyya;
segs.e: “Ānanda, suppose there was a woman or man who was young, youthful, and fond of adornments, and had bathed their head. After getting a garland of lotuses, jasmine, or liana flowers, they would take them in both hands and place them on the crown of the head.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante ānanda, ime aṭṭha garudhamme paṭiggaṇhāmi yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīye”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, sir, I accept these eight principles of respect as not to be transgressed so long as life lasts.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “paṭiggahitā, bhante, mahāpajāpatiyā gotamiyā aṭṭha garudhammā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyā”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, Mahāpajāpati Gotamī has accepted the eight principles of respect as not to be transgressed so long as life lasts.”

segs.p: “Sace, ānanda, nālabhissa mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjaṁ, ciraṭṭhitikaṁ, ānanda, brahmacariyaṁ abhavissa, vassasahassameva saddhammo tiṭṭheyya.
segs.e: “Ānanda, if ladies had not gained the going forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One, the spiritual life would have lasted long. The true teaching would have remained for a thousand years.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, ānanda, mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito, na dāni, ānanda, brahmacariyaṁ ciraṭṭhitikaṁ bhavissati.
segs.e: But since they have gained the going forth, now the spiritual life will not last long.

segs.p: Pañceva dāni, ānanda, vassasatāni saddhammo ṭhassati.
segs.e: The true teaching will remain only five hundred years.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, yāni kānici kulāni bahutthikāni appapurisakāni, tāni suppadhaṁsiyāni honti corehi kumbhatthenakehi;
segs.e: It’s like those families with many women and few men. They’re easy prey for bandits and grain-jar thieves.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, ānanda, yasmiṁ dhammavinaye labhati mātugāmo agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjaṁ, na taṁ brahmacariyaṁ ciraṭṭhitikaṁ hoti.
segs.e: In the same way, the spiritual life does not last long in a teaching and training where ladies gain the going forth.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, sampanne sālikkhette setaṭṭhikā nāma rogajāti nipatati, evaṁ taṁ sālikkhettaṁ na ciraṭṭhitikaṁ hoti;
segs.e: It’s like a field full of rice. Once the disease called ‘white bones’ attacks, it doesn’t last long.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, ānanda, yasmiṁ dhammavinaye labhati mātugāmo agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjaṁ, na taṁ brahmacariyaṁ ciraṭṭhitikaṁ hoti.
segs.e: In the same way, the spiritual life does not last long in a teaching and training where ladies gain the going forth.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, sampanne ucchukkhette mañjiṭṭhikā nāma rogajāti nipatati, evaṁ taṁ ucchukkhettaṁ na ciraṭṭhitikaṁ hoti;
segs.e: It’s like a field full of sugarcane. Once the disease called ‘red rot’ attacks, it doesn’t last long.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, ānanda, yasmiṁ dhammavinaye labhati mātugāmo agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajjaṁ, na taṁ brahmacariyaṁ ciraṭṭhitikaṁ hoti.
segs.e: In the same way, the spiritual life does not last long in a teaching and training where ladies gain the going forth.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, puriso mahato taḷākassa paṭikacceva āḷiṁ bandheyya yāvadeva udakassa anatikkamanāya;
segs.e: As a man might build a dyke around a large lake as a precaution against the water overflowing,

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, ānanda, mayā paṭikacceva bhikkhunīnaṁ aṭṭha garudhammā paññattā yāvajīvaṁ anatikkamanīyā”ti.
segs.e: in the same way as a precaution I’ve prescribed the eight principles of respect as not to be transgressed so long as life lasts.”
Numbered Discourses 8.52
6. Gotamī
An Adviser for Nuns

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “katihi nu kho, bhante, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammannitabbo”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, how many qualities should a monk have to be deemed an adviser for nuns?”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhahi kho, ānanda, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammannitabbo.
segs.e: “Ānanda, a monk with eight qualities may be deemed an adviser for nuns.
What eight?

segs.p: Idhānanda, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu;
segs.e: Firstly, a monk is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

They’re learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s totally full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reciting them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso;
segs.e: Both monastic codes have been passed down to them in detail, well analyzed, well mastered, well evaluated in both the rules and accompanying material.

segs.p: kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo, poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā;
segs.e: They’re a good speaker who enunciates well. Their voice is polished, clear, articulate, and expresses the meaning.

segs.p: paṭibalo hoti bhikkhunisaṅghassa dhammiyā kathāya sandassetuṁ samādapetuṁ samuttejetuṁ sampahaṁsetuṁ;
segs.e: They’re able to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire the community of nuns.
They’re liked and agreeable to most of the nuns.

segs.p: na kho panetaṁ bhagavantaṁ uddissa pabbajitāya kāsāyavatthavasanāya garudhammaṁ ajjhāpannapubbo hoti;
segs.e: They have never previously sexually harassed any woman wearing the ocher robe who has gone forth in the Buddha’s name.
They have been ordained for twenty years or more.

segs.p: Imehi kho, ānanda, aṭṭhahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammannitabbo”ti.
segs.e: A monk with these eight qualities may be deemed an adviser for nuns.”
Numbered Discourses 8.53
6. Gotamī
Brief Advice to Gotamī

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho mahāpajāpatī gotamī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā mahāpajāpatī gotamī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahāpajāpati Gotamī went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā ekā vūpakaṭṭhā appamattā ātāpinī pahitattā vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”
“Gotamī, you might know that certain things
lead to passion, not dispassion;
to yoking, not to unyoking;
to accumulation, not dispersal;
to more desires, not fewer;
to lack of contentment, not contentment;
to crowding, not seclusion;
to laziness, not energy;
to being burdensome, not being unburdensome.
Categorically, you should remember these things as
not the teaching, not the training, and not the Teacher’s instructions.

segs.p: Ye ca kho tvaṁ, gotami, dhamme jāneyyāsi:
segs.e: You might know that certain things
lead to dispassion, not passion;
to unyoking, not to yoking;
to dispersal, not accumulation;
to fewer desires, not more;
to contentment, not lack of contentment;
to seclusion, not crowding;
to energy, not laziness;
to being unburdensome, not being burdensome.
Categorically, you should remember these things as
the teaching, the training, and the Teacher’s instructions.”
Numbered Discourses 8.54
6. Gotamī
With Dīghajāṇu

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā koliyesu viharati kakkarapattaṁ nāma koliyānaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Koliyans, where they have a town named Kakkarapatta.

segs.p: Atha kho dīghajāṇu koliyaputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho dīghajāṇu koliyaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Dīghajāṇu the Koliyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “mayaṁ, bhante, gihī kāmabhogino puttasambādhasayanaṁ ajjhāvasāma, kāsikacandanaṁ paccanubhoma, mālāgandhavilepanaṁ dhārayāma, jātarūparajataṁ sādayāma.
segs.e: “Sir, we are laypeople who enjoy sensual pleasures and living at home with our children. We use sandalwood imported from Kāsi, we wear garlands, fragrance, and makeup, and we accept gold and currency.

segs.p: Tesaṁ no, bhante, bhagavā amhākaṁ tathā dhammaṁ desetu ye amhākaṁ assu dhammā diṭṭhadhammahitāya diṭṭhadhammasukhāya, samparāyahitāya samparāyasukhāyā”ti.
segs.e: May the Buddha please teach us the Dhamma in a way that leads to our welfare and happiness in this life and lives to come.”

segs.p: “Cattārome, byagghapajja, dhammā kulaputtassa diṭṭhadhammahitāya saṁvattanti diṭṭhadhammasukhāya.
segs.e: “Byagghapajja, these four things lead to the welfare and happiness of a gentleman in this life.
What four?
Accomplishment in initiative, protection, good friendship, and balanced finances.
And what is accomplishment in initiative?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajja, kulaputto yena kammaṭṭhānena jīvikaṁ kappeti—
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman earns a living by means such as

segs.p: yadi kasiyā, yadi vaṇijjāya, yadi gorakkhena, yadi issattena, yadi rājaporisena, yadi sippaññatarena—
segs.e: farming, trade, raising cattle, archery, government service, or one of the professions.

segs.p: tattha dakkho hoti analaso, tatrupāyāya vīmaṁsāya samannāgato, alaṁ kātuṁ alaṁ saṁvidhātuṁ.
segs.e: He understands how to go about these things in order to complete and organize the work.
This is called accomplishment in initiative.
And what is accomplishment in protection?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajja, kulaputtassa bhogā honti uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatā bāhābalaparicitā, sedāvakkhittā, dhammikā dhammaladdhā.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman owns legitimate wealth that he has earned by his own efforts and initiative, built up with his own hands, gathered by the sweat of the brow.
He ensures it is guarded and protected, thinking:

segs.p: ‘kinti me ime bhoge neva rājāno hareyyuṁ, na corā hareyyuṁ, na aggi ḍaheyya, na udakaṁ vaheyya, na appiyā dāyādā hareyyun’ti.
segs.e: ‘How can I prevent my wealth from being taken by rulers or bandits, consumed by fire, swept away by flood, or taken by unloved heirs?’
This is called accomplishment in protection.
And what is accomplishment in good friendship?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajja, kulaputto yasmiṁ gāme vā nigame vā paṭivasati, tattha ye te honti—gahapatī vā gahapatiputtā vā daharā vā vuddhasīlino, vuddhā vā vuddhasīlino, saddhāsampannā, sīlasampannā, cāgasampannā, paññāsampannā—tehi saddhiṁ santiṭṭhati sallapati sākacchaṁ samāpajjati; yathārūpānaṁ saddhāsampannānaṁ saddhāsampadaṁ anusikkhati, yathārūpānaṁ sīlasampannānaṁ sīlasampadaṁ anusikkhati, yathārūpānaṁ cāgasampannānaṁ cāgasampadaṁ anusikkhati, yathārūpānaṁ paññāsampannānaṁ paññāsampadaṁ anusikkhati.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman resides in a town or village. And in that place there are householders or their children who may be young or old, but are mature in conduct, accomplished in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom. He associates with them, converses and engages in discussion. And he emulates the same kind of accomplishment in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom.
This is called accomplishment in good friendship.
And what is accomplishment in balanced finances?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajja, kulaputto āyañca bhogānaṁ viditvā, vayañca bhogānaṁ viditvā, samaṁ jīvikaṁ kappeti nāccogāḷhaṁ nātihīnaṁ: ‘evaṁ me āyo vayaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, na ca me vayo āyaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassatī’ti.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman, knowing his income and expenditure, balances his finances, being neither too extravagant nor too frugal. He thinks, ‘In this way my income will exceed my expenditure, not the reverse.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, byagghapajja, tulādhāro vā tulādhārantevāsī vā tulaṁ paggahetvā jānāti: ‘ettakena vā onataṁ, ettakena vā unnatan’ti;
segs.e: It’s like an appraiser or their apprentice who, holding up the scales, knows that it’s low by this much or high by this much.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, byagghapajja, kulaputto āyañca bhogānaṁ viditvā, vayañca bhogānaṁ viditvā, samaṁ jīvikaṁ kappeti nāccogāḷhaṁ nātihīnaṁ: ‘evaṁ me āyo vayaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, na ca me vayo āyaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassatī’ti.
segs.e: In the same way, a gentleman, knowing his income and expenditure, balances his finances, being neither too extravagant nor too frugal. He thinks, ‘In this way my income will exceed my expenditure, not the reverse.’

segs.p: Sacāyaṁ, byagghapajja, kulaputto appāyo samāno uḷāraṁ jīvikaṁ kappeti, tassa bhavanti vattāro: ‘udumbarakhādīvāyaṁ kulaputto bhoge khādatī’ti.
segs.e: If a gentleman has little income but an opulent life, there’ll be some who say: ‘This gentleman eats their wealth like a fig-eater!’

segs.p: Sace panāyaṁ, byagghapajja, kulaputto mahāyo samāno kasiraṁ jīvikaṁ kappeti, tassa bhavanti vattāro: ‘ajeṭṭhamaraṇaṁvāyaṁ kulaputto marissatī’ti.
segs.e: If a gentleman has a large income but a spartan life, there’ll be some who say: ‘This gentleman is starving themselves to death!’

segs.p: Yato ca khoyaṁ, byagghapajja, kulaputto āyañca bhogānaṁ viditvā, vayañca bhogānaṁ viditvā, samaṁ jīvikaṁ kappeti nāccogāḷhaṁ nātihīnaṁ: ‘evaṁ me āyo vayaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, na ca me vayo āyaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassatī’ti.
segs.e: But a gentleman, knowing his income and expenditure, leads a balanced life, neither too extravagant nor too frugal, thinking, ‘In this way my income will exceed my expenditure, not the reverse.’
This is called accomplishment in balanced finances.

segs.p: Evaṁ samuppannānaṁ, byagghapajja, bhogānaṁ cattāri apāyamukhāni honti—
segs.e: There are four drains on wealth that has been gathered in this way.

segs.p: itthidhutto, surādhutto, akkhadhutto, pāpamitto pāpasahāyo pāpasampavaṅko.
segs.e: Womanizing, drinking, gambling, and having bad friends, companions, and associates.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, byagghapajja, mahato taḷākassa cattāri ceva āyamukhāni, cattāri ca apāyamukhāni.
segs.e: Suppose there was a large reservoir with four inlets and four drains.

segs.p: Tassa puriso yāni ceva āyamukhāni tāni pidaheyya, yāni ca apāyamukhāni tāni vivareyya;
segs.e: And someone was to open up the drains and close off the inlets,

segs.p: devo ca na sammā dhāraṁ anuppaveccheyya.
segs.e: and the heavens don’t provide enough rain.

segs.p: Evañhi tassa, byagghapajja, mahato taḷākassa parihāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā, no vuddhi;
segs.e: You’d expect that large reservoir to dwindle, not expand.

segs.p: evamevaṁ, byagghapajja, evaṁ samuppannānaṁ bhogānaṁ cattāri apāyamukhāni honti—
segs.e: In the same way, there are four drains on wealth that has been gathered in this way.

segs.p: itthidhutto, surādhutto, akkhadhutto, pāpamitto pāpasahāyo pāpasampavaṅko.
segs.e: Womanizing, drinking, gambling, and having bad friends, companions, and associates.

segs.p: Evaṁ samuppannānaṁ, byagghapajja, bhogānaṁ cattāri āyamukhāni honti—
segs.e: There are four inlets for wealth that has been gathered in this way.

segs.p: na itthidhutto, na surādhutto, na akkhadhutto, kalyāṇamitto kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko.
segs.e: Not womanizing, drinking, or gambling, and having good friends, companions, and associates.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, byagghapajja, mahato taḷākassa cattāri ceva āyamukhāni, cattāri ca apāyamukhāni.
segs.e: Suppose there was a large reservoir with four inlets and four drains.

segs.p: Tassa puriso yāni ceva āyamukhāni tāni vivareyya, yāni ca apāyamukhāni tāni pidaheyya;
segs.e: And someone was to open up the inlets and close off the drains,
and the heavens provide plenty of rain.

segs.p: Evañhi tassa, byagghapajja, mahato taḷākassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni;
segs.e: You’d expect that large reservoir to expand, not dwindle.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, byagghapajja, evaṁ samuppannānaṁ bhogānaṁ cattāri āyamukhāni honti—
segs.e: In the same way, there are four inlets for wealth that has been gathered in this way.

segs.p: na itthidhutto, na surādhutto, na akkhadhutto, kalyāṇamitto kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko.
segs.e: Not womanizing, drinking, or gambling, and having good friends, companions, and associates.

segs.p: Ime kho, byagghapajja, cattāro dhammā kulaputtassa diṭṭhadhammahitāya saṁvattanti diṭṭhadhammasukhāya.
segs.e: These are the four things that lead to the welfare and happiness of a gentleman in this life.

segs.p: Cattārome, byagghapajja, dhammā kulaputtassa samparāyahitāya saṁvattanti samparāyasukhāya.
segs.e: These four things lead to the welfare and happiness of a gentleman in lives to come.
What four?
Accomplishment in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom.
And what is accomplishment in faith?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajja, kulaputto saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ:
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’
This is called accomplishment in faith.
And what is accomplishment in ethics?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajja, kulaputto pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.
This is called accomplishment in ethics.
And what is accomplishment in generosity?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajja, kulaputto vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.
This is called accomplishment in generosity.
And what is accomplishment in wisdom?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajja, kulaputto paññavā hoti, udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman is wise. He has the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
This is called accomplishment in wisdom.

segs.p: Ime kho, byagghapajja, cattāro dhammā kulaputtassa samparāyahitāya saṁvattanti samparāyasukhāyāti.
segs.e: These are the four things that lead to the welfare and happiness of a gentleman in lives to come.
They’re enterprising in the workplace,
diligent in managing things,
they balance their finances,
and preserve their wealth.
Faithful, accomplished in ethics,
bountiful, rid of stinginess,
they always purify the path
to well-being in lives to come.
And so these eight qualities
of a faithful householder of discernment
are declared by the one who is truly named
to lead to happiness in both spheres,
welfare and benefit in this life,
and happiness in lives to come.
This is how, for a householder,
merit grows by generosity.”

With Ujjaya

And what is accomplishment in faith?

segs.p: Idha, brāhmaṇa, kulaputto saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ:
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’
This is called accomplishment in faith.
And what is accomplishment in ethics?

segs.p: Idha, brāhmaṇa, kulaputto pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.
This is called accomplishment in ethics.
And what is accomplishment in generosity?

segs.p: Idha, brāhmaṇa, kulaputto vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgo payatapāṇi vosaggarato yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.
This is called accomplishment in generosity.
And what is accomplishment in wisdom?

segs.p: Idha, brāhmaṇa, kulaputto paññavā hoti …pe… sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman is wise. He has the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
This is called accomplishment in wisdom.

segs.p: “Ime kho, brāhmaṇa, cattāro dhammā kulaputtassa samparāyahitāya saṁvattanti samparāyasukhāyāti.
segs.e: These are the four things that lead to the welfare and happiness of a gentleman in lives to come.
They’re enterprising in the workplace,
diligent in managing things,
they balance their finances,
and preserve their wealth.
Faithful, accomplished in ethics,
bountiful, rid of stinginess,
they always purify the path
to well-being in lives to come.
And so these eight qualities
of a faithful householder of discernment
are declared by the one who is truly named
to lead to happiness in both spheres,
welfare and benefit in this life,
and happiness in lives to come.
This is how, for a householder,
merit grows by generosity.”
Numbered Discourses 8.56
6. Gotamī
Danger
“Mendicants, ‘danger’ is a term for sensual pleasures.
‘Suffering’,
‘disease’,
‘boil’,
‘dart’,
‘chain’,
‘bog’,
and ‘womb’ are terms for sensual pleasures.
And why is ‘danger’ a term for sensual pleasures?

segs.p: Yasmā ca kāmarāgarattāyaṁ, bhikkhave, chandarāgavinibaddho diṭṭhadhammikāpi bhayā na parimuccati, samparāyikāpi bhayā na parimuccati, tasmā ‘bhayan’ti kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: Someone who is besotted by sensual greed and shackled by lustful desire is not freed from dangers in this life or in lives to come. That is why ‘danger’ is a term for sensual pleasures.
And why are ‘suffering’,
‘disease’,
‘boil’,
‘dart’,
‘chain’,
‘bog’,
and ‘womb’ terms for sensual pleasures?

segs.p: Yasmā ca kāmarāgarattāyaṁ, bhikkhave, chandarāgavinibaddho diṭṭhadhammikāpi gabbhā na parimuccati, samparāyikāpi gabbhā na parimuccati, tasmā ‘gabbho’ti kāmānametaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: Someone who is besotted by sensual greed and shackled by lustful desire is not freed from wombs in this life or in lives to come. That is why ‘womb’ is a term for sensual pleasures.
Danger, suffering, and disease,
boil, dart, and chain,
and bogs and wombs both.
These describe the sensual pleasures
to which ordinary people are attached.
Swamped by things that seem pleasant,
you go to another womb.
But when a mendicant is keen,
and doesn’t forget awareness,
in this way that sort transcend
this grueling swamp.
They watch this population flounder,
fallen into rebirth and old age.”
Numbered Discourses 8.57
6. Gotamī
Worthy of Offerings Dedicated to the Gods (1st)

segs.p: “Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with eight qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What eight?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

They’re learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s totally full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reciting them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.
They have good friends, companions, and associates.
They have right view, possessing right perspective.

segs.p: catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati;
segs.e: They recollect many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

segs.p: dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena …pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti;
segs.e: With clairvoyance that is purified and surpasses the human, they see how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.
They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these eight qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 8.58
6. Gotamī
Worthy of Offerings Dedicated to the Gods (2nd)

segs.p: “Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “A mendicant with eight qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What eight?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu;

segs.p: āraddhavīriyo viharati thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu;
segs.e: They live with energy roused up. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.
They live in the wilderness, in remote lodgings.

segs.p: aratiratisaho hoti, uppannaṁ aratiṁ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya viharati;
segs.e: They prevail over desire and discontent, and live having mastered desire and discontent whenever they arose.

segs.p: bhayabheravasaho hoti, uppannaṁ bhayabheravaṁ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya viharati;
segs.e: They prevail over fear and dread, and live having mastered fear and dread whenever they arose.

segs.p: catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.
They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these eight qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 8.59
6. Gotamī
Eight Individuals (1st)

segs.p: “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, puggalā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa?
segs.e: “Mendicants, these eight individuals are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.
What eight?

segs.p: Sotāpanno, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, sakadāgāmī, sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, anāgāmī, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, arahā, arahattāya paṭipanno.
segs.e: The stream-enterer and the one practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry. The once-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of once-return. The non-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of non-return. The perfected one, and the one practicing for perfection.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha puggalā āhuneyyā …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassāti.
segs.e: These are the eight individuals who are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.
Four practicing the path,
and four established in the fruit.
This is the upright Saṅgha,
with wisdom, ethics, and immersion.
For humans, those merit-seeking creatures,
who sponsor sacrifices,
making worldly merit,
what is given to the Saṅgha is very fruitful.”
Numbered Discourses 8.60
6. Gotamī
Eight Individuals (2nd)

segs.p: “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, puggalā āhuneyyā …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these eight individuals are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.
What eight?

segs.p: Sotāpanno, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno …pe… arahā, arahattāya paṭipanno.
segs.e: The stream-enterer and the one practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry. The once-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of once-return. The non-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of non-return. The perfected one, and the one practicing for perfection.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha puggalā āhuneyyā …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassāti.
segs.e: These are the eight individuals who are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.
Four practicing the path,
and four established in the fruit.
This is the exalted Saṅgha,
the eight individuals among sentient beings.
For humans, those merit-seeking creatures,
who sponsor sacrifices,
making worldly merit,
what’s given here is very fruitful.”
Numbered Discourses 8.61
7. Earthquakes
Desire
“Mendicants, these eight individuals are found in the world.
What eight?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pavivittassa viharato nirāyattavuttino icchā uppajjati lābhāya.
segs.e: First, when a mendicant stays secluded, living independently, a desire arises for material things.
They try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them.

segs.p: Tassa uṭṭhahato ghaṭato vāyamato lābhāya lābho nuppajjati.
segs.e: But material things don’t come to them.

segs.p: So tena alābhena socati kilamati paridevati, urattāḷiṁ kandati, sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: And so they sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion because they don’t get those material things.
This is called

segs.p: ‘bhikkhu iccho viharati lābhāya, uṭṭhahati ghaṭati vāyamati lābhāya, na ca lābhī, socī ca paridevī ca, cuto ca saddhammā’.
segs.e: a mendicant who lives desiring material things. They try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them. But when they do not acquire material things, they sorrow and lament. They’ve fallen from the true teaching.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pavivittassa viharato nirāyattavuttino icchā uppajjati lābhāya.
segs.e: Next, when a mendicant stays secluded, living independently, a desire arises for material things.
They try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them.

segs.p: Tassa uṭṭhahato ghaṭato vāyamato lābhāya lābho uppajjati.
segs.e: And material things do come to them.

segs.p: So tena lābhena majjati pamajjati pamādamāpajjati.
segs.e: And so they become indulgent and fall into negligence regarding those material things.
This is called

segs.p: ‘bhikkhu iccho viharati lābhāya, uṭṭhahati ghaṭati vāyamati lābhāya, lābhī ca madī ca pamādī ca, cuto ca saddhammā’.
segs.e: a mendicant who lives desiring material things. They try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them. And when they acquire material things, they become intoxicated and negligent. They’ve fallen from the true teaching.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pavivittassa viharato nirāyattavuttino icchā uppajjati lābhāya.
segs.e: Next, when a mendicant stays secluded, living independently, a desire arises for material things.

segs.p: So na uṭṭhahati na ghaṭati na vāyamati lābhāya.
segs.e: They don’t try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them.

segs.p: Tassa anuṭṭhahato aghaṭato avāyamato lābhāya lābho nuppajjati.
segs.e: And material things don’t come to them.

This is called

segs.e: a mendicant who lives desiring material things. They don’t try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them. And when they do not acquire material things, they sorrow and lament. They’ve fallen from the true teaching.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pavivittassa viharato nirāyattavuttino icchā uppajjati lābhāya.
segs.e: Next, when a mendicant stays secluded, living independently, a desire arises for material things.

segs.p: So na uṭṭhahati, na ghaṭati, na vāyamati lābhāya.
segs.e: They don’t try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them.

segs.e: But material things do come to them.

segs.p: So tena lābhena majjati, pamajjati, pamādamāpajjati.
segs.e: And so they become indulgent and fall into negligence regarding those material things.
This is called

segs.p: ‘bhikkhu iccho viharati lābhāya, na uṭṭhahati na ghaṭati na vāyamati lābhāya, lābhī ca madī ca, pamādī ca, cuto ca saddhammā’.
segs.e: a mendicant who lives desiring material things. They don’t try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them. But when they acquire material things, they become intoxicated and negligent. They’ve fallen from the true teaching.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pavivittassa viharato nirāyattavuttino icchā uppajjati lābhāya.

They try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them.

segs.e: But they don’t become indulgent and fall into negligence regarding those material things.
This is called

segs.p: ‘bhikkhu iccho viharati lābhāya, uṭṭhahati ghaṭati vāyamati lābhāya, lābhī ca, na ca madī na ca pamādī, accuto ca saddhammā’.

segs.e: a mendicant who lives desiring material things. They don’t try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them. And when they do not acquire material things, they don’t sorrow and lament. They haven’t fallen from the true teaching.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pavivittassa viharato nirāyattavuttino icchā uppajjati lābhāya.
segs.e: Next, when a mendicant stays secluded, living independently, a desire arises for material things.

segs.p: So na uṭṭhahati, na ghaṭati, na vāyamati lābhāya.
segs.e: They don’t try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them.

segs.p: Tassa anuṭṭhahato aghaṭato avāyamato lābhāya lābho uppajjati.
segs.e: But material things do come to them.

segs.p: So tena lābhena na majjati, na pamajjati, na pamādamāpajjati.
segs.e: But they don’t become indulgent and fall into negligence regarding those material things.
This is called

segs.p: ‘bhikkhu iccho viharati lābhāya, na uṭṭhahati, na ghaṭati, na vāyamati lābhāya, lābhī ca, na ca madī na ca pamādī, accuto ca saddhammā’.
segs.e: a mendicant who lives desiring material things. They don’t try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them. And when they acquire material things, they don’t become intoxicated and negligent. They haven’t fallen from the true teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the eight individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 8.62
7. Earthquakes
Good Enough

segs.p: “Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ attano alaṁ paresaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with six qualities is good enough for themselves and others.
What six?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khippanisanti ca hoti kusalesu dhammesu;
segs.e: A mendicant is quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings.
They readily memorize the teachings they’ve heard.
They examine the meaning of teachings they’ve memorized.
Understanding the meaning and the teaching, they practice in line with the teaching.

segs.p: kalyāṇavāco ca hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo, poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā;
segs.e: They’re a good speaker who enunciates well. Their voice is polished, clear, articulate, and expresses the meaning.

segs.p: sandassako ca hoti samādapako samuttejako sampahaṁsako sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: They educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire their spiritual companions.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ attano alaṁ paresaṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant with these six qualities is good enough for themselves and others.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ attano alaṁ paresaṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant with five qualities is good enough for themselves and others.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na heva kho khippanisanti ca hoti kusalesu dhammesu;
segs.e: A mendicant is not quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings.
They readily memorize the teachings they’ve heard.
They examine the meaning of teachings they’ve memorized.
Understanding the meaning and the teaching, they practice in line with the teaching.
They’re a good speaker. Their voice is polished, clear, articulate, and expresses the meaning.

segs.p: sandassako ca hoti samādapako samuttejako sampahaṁsako sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: They educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire their spiritual companions.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ attano alaṁ paresaṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is good enough for themselves and others.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ attano nālaṁ paresaṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant with four qualities is good enough for themselves but not for others.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khippanisanti ca hoti kusalesu dhammesu;
segs.e: A mendicant is quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings.
They readily memorize the teachings they’ve heard.
They examine the meaning of teachings they’ve memorized.
Understanding the meaning and the teaching, they practice in line with the teaching.

segs.p: no ca kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo, poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā;
segs.e: But they’re not a good speaker and do not enunciate well. Their voice isn’t polished, clear, articulate, and doesn’t express the meaning.

segs.e: A mendicant with these four qualities is good enough for themselves but not for others.

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khippanisanti ca hoti kusalesu dhammesu;
segs.e: A mendicant is quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings.
They readily memorize the teachings they’ve heard.

segs.p: no ca dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthūpaparikkhitā hoti;

segs.p: na ca atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno hoti;
segs.e: Not understanding the meaning and the teaching, they don’t practice in line with the teaching.

segs.p: kalyāṇavāco ca hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo …pe… atthassa viññāpaniyā;
segs.e: They’re a good speaker who enunciates well. Their voice is polished, clear, articulate, and expresses the meaning.
They educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire their spiritual companions.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ paresaṁ, nālaṁ attano.
